jobs.title: Radar Product Manager
jobs.description_html:
Why LeoLabs? 

At LeoLabs, we’re building the living map of activity in space. Through our proprietary global radar network and AI-enabled analytics platform, we collect millions of measurements each day on more than 25,000 objects in low Earth orbit (LEO). Our radar-powered intelligence helps protect critical assets, characterize activity in orbit, monitor emerging threats, and enable safer and more effective operations for commercial and government missions. 

We’re not just building technology—we are redefining global security, safety, and transparency in space. As orbital activity accelerates and the operating environment becomes increasingly complex, LeoLabs is a trusted partner for Space Domain Awareness, Space Traffic Management, satellite operations, and national security missions around the world. 

If you're looking to work on mission-critical challenges at the intersection of aerospace, national security, sensing, software, data, and AI, your impact starts here. This position is contingent upon final approval, with an anticipated hiring timeline beginning as early as January 2027. We are beginning the search in advance of the anticipated hiring timeline. 

LeoLabs is seeking a Radar Product Manager to lead the continued development, commercialization, and growth of our transportable radar product, our radar-based space domain awareness product. 

Our transportable radar product combines advanced radar sensing, software, data processing, and operational capabilities to provide customers with persistent, high-quality information about objects and activity in low Earth orbit. Our transportable radar product extends LeoLabs' ability to deploy sensing capability where customers need it and enables a range of commercial and government missions. 

This role sits at the intersection of customers, product strategy, radar technology, engineering, operations, deployment, and business objectives. You will be responsible for understanding customer missions and market opportunities, defining where our transportable radar product should compete, shaping the capabilities and configurations customers need, and helping turn advanced radar technology into scalable products and services customers can buy, deploy, and operate. 

The ideal candidate is a strong product thinker with both commercial and technical judgment. You should have experience working in the space industry or in a closely related aerospace or national-security environment, be comfortable working with complex hardware and software systems, and be able to translate customer missions and technical capabilities into clear product and business direction. 

What You’ll Do 

  • Own the product and business strategy for our transportable radar product, including product vision, roadmap, market positioning, prioritization, packaging, configurations, and execution
  • Develop a deep understanding of our transportable radar product customers, users, missions, workflows, operational environments, procurement considerations, and buying behavior
  • Work directly with commercial and government customers, operators, mission partners, internal stakeholders, and subject-matter experts to identify unmet needs, validate product opportunities, and determine where our transportable radar product can create differentiated value
  • Identify and prioritize market segments, mission areas, use cases, deployment models, and customer problems where our transportable radar product can create meaningful mission impact and business growth
  • Translate customer, mission, and business requirements into clear product requirements, system capabilities, configurations, interfaces, and prioritized development work
  • Partner closely with radar, hardware, software, systems, data, infrastructure, and operations teams throughout the product lifecycle, from discovery and definition through development, integration, testing, deployment, operation, and iteration
  • Make product investment decisions based on customer value, strategic differentiation, revenue potential, sensor performance, technical feasibility, operational complexity, scalability, and company priorities
  • Define how our transportable radar product capabilities, configurations, service levels, and access models are packaged and positioned so customers can clearly understand what they are buying, what mission outcomes it enables, and how it differs from other LeoLabs offerings
  • Partner with Sales, Business Development, Marketing, and Customer Success to support customer engagements, technical discussions, demonstrations, proposals, strategic pursuits, pilots, and go-to-market activities
  • Help shape pricing, packaging, service models, and commercial structures for our transportable radar product offerings in partnership with Product leadership and other business stakeholders
  • Develop a strong understanding of the tradeoffs between radar performance, deployment location, coverage, capacity, tasking, reliability, availability, maintainability, cost, and customer mission outcomes
  • Partner with Engineering and Operations to understand radar performance and identify opportunities to improve sensing capability, data quality, coverage, availability, operational efficiency, and customer value
  • Help define requirements for how customers interact with and task our transportable radar product, how measurements and data products are delivered, and how our transportable radar product integrates with customer and LeoLabs software systems
  • Maintain and communicate a clear product roadmap and ensure alignment across Product, Engineering, Radar Operations, Sales, Business Development, Customer Success, and company leadership
  • Define and monitor product, business, and operational metrics that measure customer outcomes, radar performance, availability, utilization, adoption, reliability, deployment effectiveness, revenue impact, and overall product performance
  • Lead product launches and internal enablement, ensuring that customer-facing teams can effectively explain, demonstrate, position, and sell our transportable radar product capabilities
  • Continuously evaluate competing sensing solutions, emerging radar and sensor technologies, customer acquisition trends, market developments, and evolving space and national-security requirements to identify new opportunities for our transportable radar product
  • Distinguish between one-off customer requirements and repeatable market needs, ensuring our transportable radar product evolves as a scalable product family rather than a collection of bespoke radar programs
  • Help establish and improve product management practices as LeoLabs continues to scale its product organization

What We’re Looking For 

  • 5+ years of product management experience, preferably with products involving hardware, software, data, sensing, infrastructure, or other complex technical systems
  • Professional experience working in the space industry, or in a closely related aerospace, defense, or national-security environment, with demonstrated understanding of space missions, customers, operators, or technologies
  • Demonstrated experience owning products or significant product areas from market discovery and product strategy through development, deployment, launch, adoption, and iteration
  • Strong business judgment and the ability to connect product decisions to customer mission outcomes, competitive differentiation, revenue opportunities, and company strategy
  • Strong customer orientation and experience engaging directly with customers to uncover needs, validate opportunities, and translate feedback into scalable products
  • Demonstrated ability to understand complex technical systems and translate technical capabilities, limitations, and tradeoffs into clear product direction and priorities
  • Experience working across multidisciplinary engineering teams that may include hardware, software, systems, infrastructure, data, operations, or related technical functions
  • Ability to make informed prioritization decisions across competing customer requests, market opportunities, engineering constraints, operational considerations, cost, schedule, and strategic priorities
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with engineers, operators, customers, executives, and other technical and non-technical audiences
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to use technical performance data, customer feedback, market information, and business considerations to make product decisions
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving environment where customer needs, technology, operational conditions, and market requirements can evolve quickly
  • Curiosity and willingness to develop deeper expertise in radar, RF systems, space surveillance, orbital operations, and related technical domains
  • Ability to operate with a high degree of ownership and independently drive product decisions while building alignment across multiple organizations
  • Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally to engage directly with customers, partners, deployment teams, and internal stakeholders
  • LeoLabs is a global company with customers, radar sites, partners, and users around the world, and this role will require periodic travel to understand customer missions, support key engagements and deployments, and represent the product in-market

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience with radar, RF systems, remote sensing, ground-based sensors, satellite sensors, or other advanced sensing technologies
  • Experience developing or commercializing products that integrate hardware, software, data, communications, infrastructure, and operational systems
  • Direct experience with Space Domain Awareness, Space Situational Awareness, Space Surveillance and Tracking, satellite operations, orbital analysis, or related space missions
  • Familiarity with missile warning, missile tracking, and integrated air and missile defense missions, including an understanding of how sensor performance, coverage, latency, tracking quality, and data delivery support operational warning and tracking architectures
  • Experience working with satellite operators, U.S. government space organizations, allied defense organizations, intelligence organizations, or commercial space companies
  • Familiarity with radar concepts such as detection, tracking, search, revisit rates, coverage, waveforms, beam scheduling, capacity, measurement quality, or sensor tasking
  • Familiarity with orbital mechanics, tracking data, state vectors, conjunction assessment, maneuver detection, object characterization, or other space-domain concepts
  • Experience with deployed products or infrastructure where reliability, availability, maintainability, logistics, site selection, and operational support are important product considerations
  • Experience supporting government acquisition processes, strategic pursuits, proposals, demonstrations, pilots, customer evaluations, or major program captures
  • Experience defining product packaging, pricing, configurations, service levels, or go-to-market strategy for complex technical products
  • Experience working with products sold through multiple ownership, operating, or service models
  • Experience working directly with government and commercial customers in complex enterprise sales environments
  • Technical degree or background in engineering, physics, computer science, aerospace, electrical engineering, systems engineering, or a related field
  • Active U.S. Government security clearance, or the ability and willingness to obtain and maintain one, is preferred

What Success Looks Like 

In this role, success means: 

  • Our transportable radar product has a clear product and market strategy aligned with LeoLabs' broader business objectives and differentiated from competing sensing solutions
  • The organization has a strong understanding of our transportable radar product's target customers, priority missions, deployment models, use cases, value propositions, and commercial opportunities
  • Our transportable radar product capabilities and configurations are packaged and positioned in ways that customers can easily understand, evaluate, purchase, deploy, and use
  • Our transportable radar product evolves from advanced radar technology into a scalable product family that can support multiple customer missions and business models without excessive customization
  • Engineering and Operations have clear product direction, well-defined priorities, and a strong understanding of the customer and business outcomes behind the work
  • Product decisions appropriately balance mission outcomes, radar performance, customer requirements, technical feasibility, deployment complexity, cost, schedule, and business value
  • Our transportable radar product continues to improve in areas such as sensing performance, data quality, coverage, capacity, availability, reliability, deployability, operational efficiency, and customer usability
  • Customers see measurable mission value from our transportable radar product and increasingly integrate its capabilities into their operational workflows
  • Our transportable radar product contributes meaningfully to LeoLabs' revenue growth through new deployments, new customers, expansion opportunities, strategic programs, and increased adoption
  • Sales and Business Development teams have clearly defined our transportable radar product offerings, compelling demonstrations, strong positioning, and supporting materials that allow them to confidently take our transportable radar product to market
  • Product, radar, engineering, operations, and customer-facing teams remain aligned around priorities, product configurations, upcoming capabilities, deployments, and customer commitments
  • Our transportable radar product continues to evolve based on customer outcomes, operational performance, market demand, competitive dynamics, technology advances, and LeoLabs' long-term strategy

Compensation 

This position is benchmarked to Denver, CO with a base salary range of $171,000–$194,000 plus bonus and equity. Actual base salary will be determined based on the candidate’s work location, experience, skills, and other applicable factors 
 
 Perks and Benefits  

  • 100 USD monthly wellness benefit to support your health and well-being 
  • $300 USD home office setup stipend, available for use within your first six months 
  • $75 USD monthly home internet allowance, paid directly through your regular paycheck 
  • Individual Development Fund to support training, learning, and professional development 
  • Employee Recognition Program to celebrate contributions and achievements across the team 
  • Employee Referral Program so you can help us connect with great talent 
  • And much more! 

ITAR Requirements  

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. More information regarding ITAR can be found at DDTC’s website.   

Vendor Notification 

LeoLabs does not engage external staffing agencies or third-party recruiting firms for this role. Unsolicited candidate submissions will not be considered. 

We are committed to maintaining a respectful and inclusive workplace where employees are valued for their skills, experience, and contributions. We are an equal opportunity employer and make employment decisions based on qualifications, skills, experience, and business needs, consistent with applicable law.

Why LeoLabs?

At LeoLabs, we’re building the living map of activity in space. Through our proprietary global radar network and AI-enabled analytics platform, we collect millions of measurements daily on more than 25,000 objects in low Earth orbit (LEO). Our radar-powered intelligence protects billions in assets, monitors adversarial behavior, and ensures safe operations for commercial and government missions.

We’re not just building technology, we are redefining global security, safety, and transparency in space. As orbital activity accelerates and threats grow more complex, LeoLabs is a trusted partner for Space Domain Awareness, Space Traffic Management, and Satellite Operations for top-tier space operators and allied defense organizations.

If you're looking to work on mission-critical challenges at the forefront of aerospace, national security, and AI, your impact starts here.

LeoLabs is seeking a Technical Program Manager (TPM)/Lead Systems Engineer to lead the technical execution of mission-critical programs advancing next-generation radar systems, software platforms, and data solutions for government and commercial customers supporting Space Domain Awareness (SDA), Space Superiority, and Missile Warning missions.  The TPM will serve as the primary liaison between customers, engineering teams, and program stakeholders, ensuring successful delivery of technical solutions while managing scope, schedule, risk, and performance objectives.

jobs.description_html:
AI Software Engineer

Second Front Systems is looking for an ambitious, mission-focused, full-stack AI Software Engineer to strengthen our growing Research and Development organization building AI-native platform capabilities.

Operating at the intersection of AI systems engineering and national security infrastructure, you will be responsible for designing, building, and shipping production agentic AI systems while establishing the cloud infrastructure and governance they operate within.

You will move from prototype to production across agent design, implementation, LLM integration, and cloud deployment, ensuring measurable output quality and user authorization at every stage, ensuring that Game Warden and downstream products integrate AI as foundational capability rather than feature. Your solutions will include evaluative rigor and organizational fluency.

We need someone capable of building and shipping agentic systems with LangGraph, LangChain, tool-calling, and multi-step orchestration; operating cloud infrastructure (EKS, Terraform, Helm) and LLM gateway patterns across AWS Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, self-hosted models and provider-agnostic architectures; and defining and measuring agent quality through evaluation suites, then translating results into model selection and architecture decisions.

As a key partner to our Product and Engineering teams, which are seeking to identify and deploy AI workflows across onboarding, deployment, monitoring, and remediation, you will advise on agent architecture and scope, model selection, implementation, and responsible AI governance. You will build documentation and reusable components that multiply organizational AI capability, serving as technical authority translating research-grade AI systems into mission-ready product.

Note: Candidates must reside in one of our approved hiring hubs:
• DC/Maryland/Virginia
• Denver/Colorado Springs, CO

This is a full-time position.

What You'll Do
• Architect production agentic AI systems using LangGraph and LangChain with focus on reliability, traceability, and measurable output quality.
• Build agent components including ingestion pipelines, embedding strategies, chunking, retrieval, and re-ranking, and tool suites across managed knowledge-base services, vector databases, and internal and external APIs.
• Connect agents to corporate tools and knowledge through Model Context Protocol, constructing both MCP servers and consuming clients.
• Establish and operate cloud infrastructure for R&D AI systems: Amazon EKS, Terraform, Helm, and GitOps delivery patterns.
• Measure agent and LLM output quality through evaluation and regression suites covering groundedness, faithfulness, relevance, and retrieval quality, running in CI.
• Partner with Product teams to scope high-leverage AI opportunities across workflows and advise on agent design, model selection and output quality standards.

What You Bring
• 2+ years full-time software, ML, or AI engineering experience with hands-on production work building and shipping LLM-based systems.
• Hands-on experience building agentic AI systems with tool-calling agents and multi-step orchestration using LangGraph, LangChain, or equivalent.
• Production experience with Retrieval-Augmented Generation including vector stores, embedding models, chunking strategies, and retrieval quality optimization.
• Experience deploying containerized AI services to cloud environments using Docker, Kubernetes (EKS preferred), and infrastructure as code (Terraform preferred).
• Demonstrated ability to communicate AI concepts and recommendations to non-technical stakeholders and cross-functional teams.

  • U.S. citizenship required!


    Preferred
    • Experience building MCP servers or clients, or integrating agents with enterprise tools and knowledge bases.
    • Experience with AWS AI services such as Bedrock Knowledge Bases, AgentCore, and OpenSearch.
    • Experience operating LLM gateways or serving infrastructure (e.g., LiteLLM, vLLM, GPU-backed self-hosted models), including single- and multi-tenant designs.
    • Experience driving AI adoption across a product organization: not just building, but enabling others to use AI effectively.
    • Experience working in or with the Department of Defense, federal agencies, or regulated environments, and familiarity with compliance frameworks such as NIST 800-53, FedRAMP, or NATO D32.

The base salary for this position will fall between $150,000 and $160,000. Your ultimate compensation will be determined by professional background, technical proficiency, seniority, and regional cost factors. You’ll be responsible for deploying, operating, and maintaining Game Warden across EMEA cloud environments while establishing secure, repeatable platform patterns that satisfy sovereignty and assurance requirements.

You’ll build landing zones and reference architectures using infrastructure-as-code and cloud-native tooling, keeping European deployments aligned with our global platform patterns while preserving accreditation inheritance across target environments. We need someone who can operate cloud-native infrastructure at production scale; build and maintain secure CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, and observability for regulated and potentially air-gapped environments; and produce the technical evidence and documentation needed to support applicable European security, accreditation, and regulatory requirements. As a key partner to our implementation and delivery teams, you’ll prepare production environments and hand them off with complete runbooks and technical evidence — serving as the operational bridge between platform architecture and customer deployment.

Work authorization & location: Candidates must hold citizenship in an EU member state, along with the right to work in the European Union, and be based in the EU (Remote). Unlike some of our other EU-based roles, this position requires citizenship rather than residency alone, given the security clearance and accreditation requirements tied to the systems this role supports. Candidates from any of the 27 EU member states are eligible, and you may be located anywhere in the EU.

Employment type & schedule: This is a full-time, remote position based in the EU, with compensation stated in EUR.

What You’ll Do

  • Deploy Game Warden and other Second Front products across AWS, Azure, GCP, and sovereign-cloud infrastructure in European regions, to specification.

  • Architect landing zones that satisfy sovereignty, customer-control, and GDPR requirements without single-vendor lock-in.

  • Govern Kubernetes, container runtimes, and infrastructure-as-code tooling to enforce repeatability across deployments.

  • Drive CI/CD, networking, identity, observability, and security controls against target-environment constraints and threat models.

  • Implement the technical controls and documentation required for EAL, FedRAMP, GovRAMP, NATO, UK MOD, or equivalent customer accreditation regimes.

  • Translate engineering tooling requirements into platform specifications, ensuring CI/CD, containerization, and accreditation workflows meet time-sensitive delivery windows.

  • Work with platform and engineering leads to resolve conflicts between automation, hardening, and operational constraints.

  • Sequence platform rollouts and upgrades to minimize disruption to active development while maintaining compliance posture and system hardening.

What You Bring

  • 5+ years of hands-on platform engineering, DevSecOps, cloud infrastructure, SRE, or systems engineering experience in production environments.

  • Deep fluency with AWS, Azure, GCP, or equivalent cloud platforms operating at scale.

  • Production-grade Kubernetes and container orchestration experience in live systems.

  • Hands-on experience writing and maintaining infrastructure-as-code with Terraform, CloudFormation, or Pulumi.

  • A track record building, securing, and operating CI/CD pipelines under regulatory or high-assurance compliance requirements.

  • Working knowledge of networking, IAM, SAML/OAuth, APIs, and distributed-systems troubleshooting in production.

  • Fluent English and a proven ability to collaborate asynchronously across distributed global engineering teams.

  • EU citizenship (any of the 27 EU member states) and the right to work in the EU.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Existing government or NATO security clearance, or eligibility to obtain one.

  • Experience operating in air-gapped, classified, or other high-assurance environments.

  • Familiarity with EAL/Common Criteria, FedRAMP, GovRAMP, NATO, or UK MOD accreditation processes; and/or familiarity with other frameworks such as NIS-2, CRA, etc.

  • Proficiency in a systems or scripting language (e.g., Go, Python, or Rust) for building internal tooling.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary for this position will fall between €120,000 and €140,000. Your ultimate compensation will be determined by professional background, technical proficiency, seniority, and regional cost factors. This role is also eligible for equity awards and discretionary bonuses as part of a broader total rewards package.

Equal Opportunity

jobs.title: Product Manager II (U.S. Air Force)
jobs.description_html:
About Skylight

Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services. 

We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world.

If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists.

The work we do matters.

About the job

At Skylight, product managers are responsible for strategy, planning, execution, stakeholder management, and team health. Product managers partner with researchers, designers, engineers, client stakeholders, and others to inform their product decisions. At a high level, it’s the product manager’s job to figure out what to build next and why.

Skylight is partnering with a U.S. Air Force program office that runs a portfolio of civil engineering systems. These systems serve users across civil engineering, security forces, and services, including readiness managers, range personnel, and fire and emergency services. Releases are slow today. Regression testing is manual, security review happens after development finishes, and code freeze to production can take a month or more. We’ll move the program to an outcome-driven model with test automation and security built into the pipeline, starting with migrating the first application onto a DoD software factory. Leadership wants this office to become the model other Air Force offices adopt.

In this role, you’ll keep the team’s delivery organized and moving, working hand in hand with the engagement manager on deliverables and documentation and owning the backlog as the program changes how it works.

What to know going in

This is an execution-focused product role, well suited to someone with a strong project management or operations instinct. Your first 30 days are about getting to know the Skylight team and government personnel, learning how work gets tracked and delivered today, and helping move the team’s backlog and documentation from Jira and Confluence to GitLab and Mattermost. Expect to work alongside government staff and other contractors, with tools and processes changing as the work gets underway.

This role is contingent on Skylight being awarded the underlying contract. If we’re not awarded the contract, we’ll let you know promptly and discuss whether there are other opportunities that fit.

What you’ll do

  • Partner with the engagement manager to organize deliverables, documentation, and schedules so the work stays on track and visible to government partners
  • Maintain a prioritized backlog: write user stories, keep priorities current, and build release plans with the team
  • Lead the team’s move from Jira and Confluence to GitLab and Mattermost, keeping configuration, tracking, and documentation clean through the transition
  • Facilitate team ceremonies such as planning meetings, stakeholder syncs, and retrospectives
  • Translate needs from users and government partners into product objectives, measures of success, and roadmap items
  • Work in close partnership with government teams to transfer digital skills and product knowledge throughout the project

What we’re looking for

Basic qualifications

  • Understand lean product principles and how to apply them (e.g., minimum viable product) at various stages of the product life cycle in order to mitigate risk, validate assumptions, and amplify learning
  • Can develop a product strategy that is informed by an understanding of the problem to be solved, prioritizes outcomes over feature sets, and establishes the direction of the product over time (e.g., product roadmap), including success criteria
  • Ability to execute the product strategy by breaking down the product’s scope into usable chunks of value that can be realized sooner rather than later, creating and maintaining a prioritized backlog with validated user stories, and facilitating team ceremonies over the course of the product’s iterations
  • Understand how to engage in the process of human-centered design in order to better inform product direction
  • Ability to collaborate with folks outside of your discipline, such as researchers, designers, engineers, and others, in order to get things done
  • Ability to manage clients and stakeholders in a way that builds trust, alignment, and healthy environments for individuals and teams
  • Understand the merits of different software development methodologies (e.g., agile, lean) and how to put them into practice
  • Strong organizational skills, with experience keeping deliverables, documentation, and action items on track for an agile software delivery team
  • Experience working on cross-functional teams (product, design, engineering, ops) in iterative delivery
  • A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values

Nice-to-haves

  • Project management experience, such as running schedules, risks, and dependencies for a delivery team
  • Configuration management experience, or experience migrating a team’s tools and workflows (for example, from Jira and Confluence to GitLab)
  • Experience with legacy modernization, or launching a new product from zero to one
  • Consulting experience, or military or Department of Defense experience
  • Experience delivering technology in government, regulated industries, or other public-benefit settings
  • A track record of staying aligned and accountable on remote teams

Don’t meet every qualification but think you can do the job? We’d still love to hear from you. If you’re excited about the role, apply. We consider candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences.

Other requirements

  • Some of our available roles are on federal contracts that require a degree or additional years of experience as a substitute.
  • All work must be conducted within the U.S., excluding U.S. territories.
  • This contract requires U.S. citizenship to be eligible for employment.
  • You must be able to obtain a Common Access Card (CAC) and any special access required for this contract.
  • You must complete a company background check successfully.

Logistics

Position type

This is a full-time, exempt position.

Location

This is a fully remote position.

Travel

This role includes occasional travel to Montgomery, AL, and other U.S. Air Force bases.

Expected start date

We’re targeting a start date of November 30, 2026, pending contract award.

Care package

Salary

We want to give you the most competitive salary possible. After all, you deserve it! To that end, we use the results of our interview process to determine what salary is most appropriate given your current level of seniority. For a Product Manager at Skylight, the current salary ranges are as follows:

  • Associate Product Manager: $90,000–$125,000
  • Product Manager I: $120,000–$140,000
  • Product Manager II: $135,000–$160,000
  • Senior Product Manager: $150,000–$185,000
  • Staff Product Manager: $170,000–$203,000
  • Principal Product Manager: $180,000–$230,000

Benefits

Your well-being is important to us, so we focus on supporting you in a variety of ways:

  • Medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability insurance
  • Life and AD&D insurance
  • Dependent care FSA, healthcare FSA, health savings account
  • Dollar-for-dollar 401(k) match up to 10% of your salary with no vesting period
  • Flexible paid-time-off policy (generally around 25 days per year), plus 11 paid federal holidays
  • Up to 12 weeks paid-time-off for all eligible new birth, adoption, or foster parents
  • Performance rewards, including annual salary increase, annual performance bonus, spot bonuses, and stock options
  • Business development / sales bonuses
  • Referral bonuses
  • Annual $2,000 allowance for professional development
  • Annual $750 allowance for tech-related purchases
  • Annual swag budget of $100 to display your Skylight pride with some merchandise (hoodies, hats, and more)
  • Flexible, remote-friendly work environment
  • An environment that empowers you to unleash your superpowers for public good

Interview tips

Our process includes a preliminary screen, a skills interview, a behavioral interview, and a reverse interview where you meet your potential team — usually four conversations across two to three weeks. Here are some tips to help you prepare for a successful interview:

  • Visit our join page to learn more about how our interview process works.
  • Check out our Career Pathways framework to learn more about the different roles within Skylight and the skills needed to do them.
  • Browse our case studies to learn more about our work.

If you’d like to request reasonable accommodations during the application or interviewing process, please contact our recruiting team at recruiting@skylight.digital.

We participate in E-Verify and upon hire, will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you’re authorized to work in the U.S.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, disability, veteran status, or any other category protected by applicable law.

A technical product manager specializes in products with significant technical depth — platforms, APIs, data systems, or modernization efforts — where product decisions depend on fluency with the underlying architecture and engineering tradeoffs.

The Administration for Children and Families (ACF) is expanding surge support and capacity for its new Data Capacity and Digital Services organization within the Office of Administration, through the option year of our Task Order 1 contract. The team works with enterprise-serving organizations like ACF Tech and the Office of Grants Management to help programs deliver on ACF’s mission, including priorities focused on reducing grantee burden; reducing waste, fraud, and abuse; and modernizing legacy systems. 

You’ll lead product work that spans rapid-turnaround surge requests and signature modernization efforts, working directly with ACF staff to decide what’s worth building and why. Much of this work sits on top of platforms like Palantir Foundry, Databricks, and enterprise AI tools, so you’ll need technical fluency to weigh architecture and data tradeoffs alongside your engineers.

This work calls for a consultant’s skill set: you’ll interface directly with senior leaders, and much of the work isn’t scoped in advance. This isn’t a team where you simply prioritize existing work in a backlog. You’ll need a working understanding of service design and fluency to engage with AI-forward delivery teams, including data scientists, Foundry engineers designers and others. Alongside delivery, we do a lot of technical consulting and capacity building, so people who take initiative and are comfortable with uncertainty and ambiguity tend to do best here.

  • Experience applying service design methods, such as journey mapping, service blueprinting, and contextual inquiry, to uncover pain points, manual workarounds, and opportunities to automate or streamline
  • Hands-on experience delivering AI-enabled products or workflows, including judging where AI (e.g., LLMs, agents, intelligent document processing) adds value versus where simpler automation or process change is the better answer
  • Understanding of how data moves through an organization, with the ability to spot fragmented or duplicated data and work with engineers to design more connected, reliable systems
  • Technical fluency to reason through system architecture, APIs, data modeling, security, and engineering tradeoffs with engineers, and to make product calls that depend on them
  • Ability to manage clients and stakeholders in a way that builds trust, alignment, and healthy environments for individuals and teams
  • A track record of defining and measuring impact, such as time saved, reduced processing times, fewer errors, or increased adoption
  • A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Technical (HHS)
jobs.description_html:
About Skylight

Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services. 

We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world.

If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists. 

The work we do matters.

About the job

At Skylight, product managers are responsible for strategy, planning, execution, stakeholder management, and team health. Product managers partner with researchers, designers, engineers, client stakeholders, and others to inform product decisions. At a high level, it’s the product manager’s job to figure out what to build next, why it matters, and how to turn that direction into something a multidisciplinary team can deliver.

A technical product manager specializes in work with significant technical depth — enterprise platforms, cloud environments, APIs, data systems, integrations, and application modernization — where product decisions depend on understanding the underlying architecture, operational constraints, and engineering tradeoffs.

Skylight supports HHS’s Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) across a growing portfolio of high-visibility digital modernization work. New initiatives can arrive quickly and without fully defined requirements, users, technical approaches, or implementation plans. We need a Staff Product Manager who can bring structure to that ambiguity and help HHS move from a problem or mandate to an actionable strategy, roadmap, and delivered outcome.

The work spans two related areas:

  • Enterprise platform optimization. Helping HHS make better use of enterprise platforms by identifying shared needs across Divisions, shaping platform and integration strategies, establishing scalable patterns, and supporting adoption of shared services.
  • Modern digital services and applications. Leading multidisciplinary teams that design, build, launch, and continuously improve production-ready digital services and applications — from early discovery and prototypes through enterprise-scale implementation and ongoing operations.

You’ll own one or more workstreams and flex between strategic product leadership and hands-on delivery. Depending on the initiative, you may help define an emerging enterprise platform strategy, conduct discovery with HHS Divisions, turn an operational problem into a product roadmap, guide a prototype toward production, or lead the continued development of an existing digital service.

What to know going in

This is not a role where every project arrives with a defined product, backlog, technical architecture, or implementation plan.

Some workstreams will begin with questions like: What problem are we actually trying to solve? Which HHS Divisions need this capability? Should this be a shared enterprise service or a Division-specific solution? What already exists? What should we standardize? What should we build? And what should happen first?

Others will involve existing applications that already have users and stakeholders and need to move quickly through feature development, integration, launch, adoption, and ongoing improvement.

You’ll need to be comfortable operating at both levels.

At the enterprise level, you may work with architects, engineers, platform owners, and HHS stakeholders to understand how platforms; identify opportunities for shared services and tenant integration; define priorities and adoption strategies; and translate technical possibilities and constraints into decisions leaders can act on.

At the product level, you’ll work closely with designers, researchers, and engineers to turn user and operational needs into working software. Current and emerging application work may include enterprise mentoring, security tooling and analytics, employee onboarding, and other internal digital services.

Across both areas, speed matters. You should be comfortable learning enough to act, showing early work, testing assumptions, and refining the approach as the team learns rather than waiting for perfect information before moving forward.

What you’ll do

  • Help federal stakeholders align and make decisions
  • Build and own the roadmap for digital services, from first prototype to a products HHS & Divisions rely on
  • Work through technical decisions with engineers
  • Translate needs from leadership and government partners into a product vision, objectives, and measures of success
  • Ship early prototypes, gather feedback, and iterate quickly rather than waiting for complete requirements
  • Write user stories, prioritize the backlog, and build release plans

What we’re looking for

Basic qualifications

  • Understand lean product principles and how to apply them (e.g., minimum viable product) at various stages of the product life cycle in order to mitigate risk, validate assumptions, and amplify learning
  • Can develop a product strategy that is informed by an understanding of the problem to be solved, prioritizes outcomes over feature sets, and establishes the direction of the product over time (e.g., product roadmap), including success criteria
  • Ability to execute the product strategy by breaking down the product’s scope into usable chunks of value that can be realized sooner rather than later, creating and maintaining a prioritized backlog with validated user stories, and facilitating team ceremonies over the course of the product’s iterations
  • Understand how to engage in the process of human-centered design in order to better inform product direction
  • Ability to collaborate with folks outside of your discipline, such as researchers, designers, engineers, and others, in order to get things done
  • Ability to manage clients and stakeholders in a way that builds trust, alignment, and healthy environments for individuals and teams
  • Understand the merits of different software development methodologies (e.g., agile, lean) and how to put them into practice
  • Product experience with data ingestion and normalization across many sources (APIs, batch exports, streaming), and enough technical depth to work through warehouse and data modeling tradeoffs with data engineers
  • Experience working on cross-functional teams (product, design, engineering, ops) in iterative delivery
  • A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience with multi-tenant cloud environments, enterprise platform consolidation, tenant rationalization, shared services, or cross-organizational platform adoption.
  • Experience delivering data and analytics products, including data ingestion, APIs, data pipelines, warehouses or lakehouses, data modeling, and access controls.
  • Experience developing or implementing enterprise integration patterns, including identity and access management, single sign-on, APIs, and data-sharing workflows.
  • Experience taking a prototype or internal tool through production hardening, launch, and ongoing operations.
  • Experience modernizing legacy applications or replacing manual business processes with digital services.
  • Experience supporting organizational change, product adoption, migrations, or onboarding to shared technology services.
  • Experience delivering technology in government, regulated industries, large federated organizations, or other public-benefit settings.
  • Experience working with federal CIO organizations or enterprise IT organizations where technology ownership and decision-making are distributed across multiple components or business units.
  • A track record of staying aligned and accountable on remote teams

Don’t meet every qualification but think you can do the job? We’d still love to hear from you. If you’re excited about the role, apply. We consider candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences.

Other requirements

  • Some of our available roles are on federal contracts that require a degree or additional years of experience as a substitute.
  • All work must be conducted within the U.S., excluding U.S. territories.
  • You must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. now and in the future without sponsorship.
  • You must be able to obtain and maintain a public trust clearance.
  • You must complete a company background check successfully.

Logistics

Position type

This is a full-time, exempt position.

Location

This is a fully remote position.

Travel

This role is remote, but occasional travel to DC may come up.

Expected start date

As soon as possible

Care package

Salary

We want to give you the most competitive salary possible. After all, you deserve it! To that end, we use the results of our interview process to determine what salary is most appropriate given your current level of seniority. For a Product Manager at Skylight, the current salary ranges are as follows:

  • Associate Product Manager: $90,000–$125,000
  • Product Manager I: $120,000–$140,000
  • Product Manager II: $135,000–$160,000
  • Senior Product Manager: $150,000–$185,000
  • Staff Product Manager: $170,000–$203,000
  • Principal Product Manager: $180,000–$230,000

Benefits

Your well-being is important to us, so we focus on supporting you in a variety of ways:

  • Medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability insurance
  • Life and AD&D insurance
  • Dependent care FSA, healthcare FSA, health savings account
  • Dollar-for-dollar 401(k) match up to 10% of your salary with no vesting period
  • Flexible paid-time-off policy (generally around 25 days per year), plus 11 paid federal holidays
  • Up to 12 weeks paid-time-off for all eligible new birth, adoption, or foster parents
  • Performance rewards, including annual salary increase, annual performance bonus, spot bonuses, and stock options
  • Business development / sales bonuses
  • Referral bonuses
  • Annual $2,000 allowance for professional development
  • Annual $750 allowance for tech-related purchases
  • Annual swag budget of $100 to display your Skylight pride with some merchandise (hoodies, hats, and more)
  • Flexible, remote-friendly work environment
  • An environment that empowers you to unleash your superpowers for public good

Interview tips

Our process includes a preliminary screen, a skills interview, a behavioral interview, and a reverse interview where you meet your potential team — usually four conversations across two to three weeks. Here are some tips to help you prepare for a successful interview:

  • Visit our join page to learn more about how our interview process works.
  • Check out our Career Pathways framework to learn more about the different roles within Skylight and the skills needed to do them.
  • Browse our case studies to learn more about our work.

If you’d like to request reasonable accommodations during the application or interviewing process, please contact our recruiting team at recruiting@skylight.digital.

We participate in E-Verify and upon hire, will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you’re authorized to work in the U.S.

jobs.title: DevOps Engineer
jobs.location: Remote; Washington, District of Columbia, United States
jobs.description_html:
Vannevar builds AI systems for the Department of War's most consequential missions. We have 125 deployments across every branch and combatant command spanning our core platform and five distinct products. An an example of how we work, when major combat operations started with Iran, we fielded a new product supporting 24/7 operations and 9,000+ users in three months.

How we build is our advantage: we deploy forward with the people who own the mission. Our engineers, product team, and CTO deploy forward to the point of friction, including visiting units in Ukraine. We focus on embedding directly with operational units supporting great power competition with China, combat operations with Iran, and counter-narcotics missions.

About the role

We are looking for a DevOps Engineer to own build and deployment automation for Vannevar Labs. Your decisions today will have a large impact on the company’s future. We believe that simple systems are easier to understand, maintain, and scale. You will be making trade-offs as you work to ensure that our systems are prepared to operate in both commercial and high-side environments at scale — being able to effectively communicate these trade-offs with your teammates is a must.
 
What you'll do
  • Develop, maintain, and be responsible for overall platform health, scaling and planning.
  • Developing self-service tools and automating things to improve data engineering efficiency.
  • Build logging and monitoring tools to visualize the state of the platform and improve our SRE practices.
  • Play a critical part in implementing a secure, robust and high availability DevOps pipeline.
  • Work with the team to continue the build out of a multi-account AWS environment.
  • Automate build & deployment processes.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in DevOps, software engineering.
  • Experience crafting CI/CD processes and automation.
  • Deep knowledge in AWS cloud technology.
  • Experience with PLG stack, Datadog, or other enterprise monitoring tools.
  • Familiarity with infrastructure as code technologies such as Terraform and Pulumi.
  • Proficient with containerization technologies like Docker.
  • Excellent with Python, Bash, or other scripting languages.
  • Experience working in an agile scrum environment and also an ability to work independently.
  • Able to quickly learn new and existing technologies.
  • Strong attention to detail and excellent analytical capabilities.
  • U.S. Citizenship status is required as this position will require the ability to access U.S. only data systems and export-controlled data.
  • TS/SCI with FSP Clearance required
  • Ability to commute/travel to DC customer site up to 50% of the time

Additional Qualifications (Nice to haves)

  • Experience working in AWS GovCloud.
  • Experience in data processing with the Department of Defense and/or the IC.
  • Experience building CD/CI systems in Github Actions.
  • Passion for DevSecOps.
  • Experience working with Elasticsearch/Opensearch.
  • Have worked hardening and delivering software applications.
  • Experience with modern web services architectures.
  • Experience with relational database systems, including SQL and relational design.
  • Knowledge of advanced networking concepts such as overlays, VPNs, and zero trust networks.
  • Strong collaboration and negotiation skills and must be able to work on multi-functional projects with internal partner engineering teams

The base salary range for this position is $160,000 - $240,000. We hire engineers at multiple levels based on their experience, technical capabilities, and scope of responsibility. This range reflects the base salaries we typically expect to offer for this role, with individual offers determined by the candidate's qualifications and level.

Equity is offered in addition to base salary.

What we offer

We’re proud to offer competitive benefits that support our employees. Some key highlights of our benefits package include:
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • 100% remote first culture. You can work from anywhere in the US and all full time employees have WeWork access
  • Unlimited PTO including competitive vacation and holiday schedules
  • Lifestyle stipends - Monthly mental health, wellness & fitness stipend, in-home office setup stipend and family planning assistance
  • Salary top-up during military reserve duty
  • Fully paid parental leave
  • Child and pet care reimbursement during travel

 

Vannevar is an equal opportunity employer, and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status.
 
We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply, even if you don't feel like you're a perfect fit. If you're passionate about contributing to our mission, we'd love to hear from you!
 
IMPORTANT NOTICE
We are committed to protecting the privacy of all applicants. Official emails from the company will come from an @vannevarlabs.com domain. Under no circumstances will a legitimate representative from our company contact you to request passwords, financial information, or other sensitive personal data. Please be vigilant of potential scams.

jobs.title: Product Manager - Digital Forensics (Clearance Required)
jobs.description_html:
Vannevar builds AI systems for the Department of War's most consequential missions. We have 125 deployments across every branch and combatant command spanning our core platform and five distinct products. An an example of how we work, when major combat operations started with Iran, we fielded a new product supporting 24/7 operations and 9,000+ users in three months.

How we build is our advantage: we deploy forward with the people who own the mission. Our engineers, product team, and CTO deploy forward to the point of friction, including visiting units in Ukraine. We focus on embedding directly with operational units supporting great power competition with China, combat operations with Iran, and counter-narcotics missions.

ABOUT THE ROLE 

We’re hiring a Product Manager for our Digital Forensics team. 

This team builds AI-driven intelligence capabilities that turn large, messy, real-world datasets into clear answers and actions for operators and investigators. The product has strong traction and is entering a period of rapid growth – many more users and far higher volume, fast. We’re hiring the PM who will own it through that scale-up. 

This is not a traditional roadmap role. You will take in incomplete, conflicting inputs from users, customers, stakeholders, and the product itself, and decide what we should build – and what we shouldn’t – as demand accelerates. 

You will work closely with operators, product engineers, forward deployed engineers, and mission colleagues to find high-leverage problems and drive them through a shipped capability. You’ll often need to set aside loud or conflicting inputs and make calls others disagree with. 

This role reports to the CTO and operates at the intersection of mission, product, and engineering. Success is measured by whether we build the right things and those things create real mission impact at scale. 

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Own the product direction end-to-end. Turn ambiguous problems into concrete bets and drive them through to shipped capability. 
  • Navigate rapid growth. Guide the product through a steep rise in users and usage, making the tradeoffs to keep it fast, focused, and reliable at scale. 
  • Turn signal into direction. Take messy, often conflicting input from users, stakeholders, and the product itself, decide what actually matters for growth and mission impact, and translate it into clear product direction – including pushing back when the loudest ask isn’t the right one. 
  • Build alignment across Mission and Engineering. Bring people along when Mission and Engineering see a problem differently – disagree when you need to, then get everyone committed on the path forward. 
  • Partner with engineering. Embed with the team, meet them where they work best, and shape solutions that are both impactful and technically sound. 
  • Work directly with users. Build deep intuition for real-world workflows and needs. 
  • Drive adoption and durability. Move users from first use to daily reliance and keep quality high as volume grows. 

WHAT YOU SHOULD HAVE 

  • Strong product judgment. You consistently identify the right problems and make sound prioritization decisions. 
  • Product experience through a growth phase. You’ve owned a product through rising users and usage, not just early 0-to-1. 
  • Ability to separate signal from noise. You form independent, defensible opinions from incomplete and conflicting inputs, and can act on them under uncertainty.  
  • Experience operating under real constraints. You’ve shipped products where security, infrastructure, or deployment realities shaped decisions. 
  • High ownership and a bias toward action. You take responsibility for outcomes and push work through to completion.  
  • Technical fluency. You can engage with engineers and understand system constraints and tradeoffs. 
  • Clear, direct communication. You can articulate decisions, tradeoffs, and reasoning in a way others can act on. 
  • Active TS/SCI clearance (or ability to obtain one) 
  • Willingness to travel onsite 

Nice to have 

  • Experience working with operational, mission-driven, or investigative users 
  • Experience with LLM-based systems 
  • Experience with product analytics (e.g., SQL) 
  • Experience rapidly prototyping ideas (Figma, AI coding tools, etc.) 
  • Experience with digital forensics or investigations 
  • Exposure to constrained or high-security environments 

What we offer

We’re proud to offer competitive benefits that support our employees. Some key highlights of our benefits package include:
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • 100% remote first culture. You can work from anywhere in the US and all full time employees have WeWork access
  • Unlimited PTO including competitive vacation and holiday schedules
  • Lifestyle stipends - Monthly mental health, wellness & fitness stipend, in-home office setup stipend and family planning assistance
  • Salary top-up during military reserve duty
  • Fully paid parental leave
  • Child and pet care reimbursement during travel

This team owns the systems that turn user intent into execution - from chat and tasking to persistent agent workflows. You will define how users delegate work to software, how those systems operate on real-world data, and how they are monitored, constrained, and improved over time.

This is not a traditional roadmap role. You will take in incomplete, conflicting inputs from users, stakeholders, data, and systems - and decide what we should actually build.

You will work closely with operators, forward deployed engineers, and engineering teams to identify high-leverage problems and drive them through to shipped capability. You will often need to ignore loud or conflicting inputs and make decisions that others disagree with.

What you should have

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Security
jobs.description_html:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

Security isn't a feature at 1Password. It is the product. We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to shape security strategy across the company, working with Security Engineering, who hold one of the highest technical bars in the industry, and with the product teams building everything our customers touch.

You'll be the bridge. You'll understand cryptographic and architectural detail well enough to earn the trust of our security engineers, and you'll translate what matters into clear priorities for feature teams. Just as importantly, you'll bring a deep respect for the customer: a security control nobody can stand to use makes everyone less safe. You'll help us find the design that's both rigorous and usable, and have the credibility to say so in a room full of experts

What you'll do

  • Partner with product teams on security early. Work with PMs and feature teams to understand their upcoming roadmaps, identify security requirements and threat-model implications before designs are locked, and make sure those needs are visible, prioritized, and resourced.

  • Align Security Engineering with product strategy. Translate feature-team needs into prioritized security work, and make Security Engineering's priorities legible to the rest of the company so tradeoffs are made in the open.

  • Own an independent security roadmap. Set direction for platform-level security investments, such as key management and recovery, the cryptographic foundations of our zero-knowledge architecture, authentication, and our long-term readiness for post-quantum cryptography.

  • Lead our strategy for the AI era. Define how 1Password approaches agentic access to credentials, secrets for non-human identities and AI agents, and the trust models emerging around tools and protocols like MCP.

  • Balance risk and usability with evidence. Help security engineers weigh real-world risk against user friction, using adoption, support, and telemetry data alongside threat models. Shipping with accepted, documented residual risk is sometimes the right call, and you'll help us make and defend those decisions.

  • Represent 1Password to the security community. Engage with security researchers and our bug bounty program, speak at conferences, and contribute to the wider conversation about where credential security is heading.

  • Raise the bar for product work. Coach PMs on security thinking, challenge assumptions constructively, and set the standard for how security-critical product work gets done.

Our philosophy on Product consists of five core pillars:

  • Focus and execution: Can you ship quickly and measure results?

  • Customer empathy: Are you motivated first and foremost to solve customer problems?

  • Effective communication: Can you bring the entire organization, horizontally and vertically, along on the journey?

  • Go to market: Can you understand and drive business outcomes through product decisions?

  • Technology: Articulating how our technology beats our competitors

Product Managers play a highly visible role at 1Password and are critical to the development and execution of our product strategy. As PMs, we are responsible for setting and championing a high bar for our products. At the Principal level, you also set the standard for how product work gets done. You coach, you challenge assumptions, and you make the whole team better. You must excel at prioritization, collaboration, and communication, while holding yourself and others accountable for measuring quality and business results. You will work with Engineering, Design, Security Research, and GTM teams to ensure every decision we make as a product is grounded in our commitment to verifiable security.

What we're looking for

  • 10+ years of product management experience, including significant time on security-critical products or platforms in a SaaS environment. We'll also strongly consider exceptional candidates with equivalent depth, such as security engineers or researchers who moved into product.

  • Deep, demonstrable knowledge of security fundamentals: cryptography, authentication protocols, identity and access management, zero-knowledge and end-to-end encrypted system design, and threat modeling.

  • Fluency in the credential and identity landscape, including passkeys, WebAuthn/FIDO, and the standards shaping how people sign in.

  • A track record of earning credibility with security engineering teams, not just working alongside them.

  • The ability to read and reason through technical specifications, security audits, and cryptographic design documents.

  • Experience making and defending risk-based tradeoffs, and explaining them clearly to engineers, executives, and customers.

  • A history of shipping security features that users actually adopt, and of using friction and adoption data to improve them.

  • Experience setting strategy at the platform or infrastructure level, and influencing roadmaps you don't own without formal authority.

  • Communication that scales from a security research paper to an executive briefing without losing precision in either direction.

  • A strong point of view on how the security landscape is shifting, and the ability to connect it to concrete roadmap decisions.

Strong plus

  • Standing in the security community, through conference talks, publications, research, open-source work, or standards participation.

  • Hands-on experience with AI security: agent identity and authorization, prompt injection, secrets management for automated systems.

  • Experience with compliance and certification regimes such as SOC 2, FedRAMP, or FIPS.

  • Prior work in vulnerability disclosure, incident response, or threat intelligence that gives you a practitioner's intuition.

  • Experience running or working closely with a bug bounty program or researcher community.

What you can expect

  • Working with a passionate, highly motivated Product and Security team that holds an exceptional bar and genuinely cares about getting it right

  • A direct line to decisions that shape the security architecture millions of people depend on every day

  • Empowerment to set long-term security product strategy and drive it through execution

  • A culture where technical depth is respected, tradeoffs are named honestly, and shipping the right thing matters more than shipping fast

You decide where the organization invests, define the architecture and standards that every infrastructure team and internal tenant builds on, and make sure our compute, network and edge, and stateful platforms evolve as one coherent system rather than three separate ones. You partner with engineering and product leadership, security, and finance to balance reliability, security, cost, and delivery speed, and you are the senior technical voice for infrastructure across the company.

This is a hands-on role. You write design docs, prototype, review the hardest designs, and step into the most serious incidents. But your main impact comes from making many teams more effective and from the decisions that hold up for years.

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

What we're looking for:

  • You have set technical direction across multiple teams. You have owned an infrastructure strategy or architecture spanning several teams or an entire organization, and you can point to the multi-year outcomes: what others adopted, what shipped, and what measurably improved.

  • You have operated Kubernetes at production scale. This includes multi-cluster, multi-tenant, customer-traffic-bearing environments (EKS or similar managed platforms preferred). You know it deeply, from autoscaling and admission control to GitOps, workload identity, and fleet-wide cluster upgrades.

  • You combine depth with breadth. Beyond Kubernetes, you have working fluency in networking and edge and in stateful data systems, and you understand how a decision in one layer affects the rest.

  • You have made reliability a standard, not a project. You defined SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets, and you got multiple teams to adopt them. You have improved incident response, post-incident learning, and disaster recovery across an organization, not just on your own team.

  • You have cut cloud costs through engineering. You can show measurable, real-dollar impact from work such as capacity automation, right-sizing, architecture changes, or commitment strategy, and you have worked with finance on forecasting and tradeoffs.

  • You build security in by design. You have driven practices such as workload identity, least-privilege IAM and RBAC, credential rotation, and strong isolation in multi-tenant environments, and you have partnered with security teams on risk decisions and compliance requirements.

  • You still build. You are proficient in Go (or a similar language) and Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), and you have a track record of automating complex, high-toil operational workflows at fleet scale.

  • You influence without relying on authority. You write clear strategy and design documents, present to senior leaders, resolve technical disagreements between teams, and build alignment on difficult tradeoffs.

  • You grow other engineers. You have mentored Senior and Staff engineers, raised the bar on design review, and helped shape how your organization hires and evaluates technical talent.

  • Hands-on experience with service mesh and service-to-service networking, such as Linkerd or Amazon VPC Lattice.

  • Experience operating scalable database technology, such as MySQL, Postgres, or DynamoDB.

  • Designing developer platform abstractions for internal teams, such as paved-road service toolkits and production readiness frameworks, that measurably improved usability and productivity.

  • Helping build AI-assisted operations tools, such as auto-remediation or AI-assisted diagnosis, rather than only using them.

  • Operating highly available, multi-region services in a large SaaS environment, including capacity planning and performance optimization at scale.

  • Experience in a security, identity, or other high-trust product environment.

What you can expect:

  • Set the multi-year technical strategy and architecture for Infrastructure Services, working with directors and senior engineering leadership to shape roadmap and investment decisions, including build versus buy.

  • Define the patterns, standards, and guardrails across compute, network and edge, and stateful services that internal teams depend on for years.

  • Represent Infrastructure Services in cross-organization reviews with product engineering, security, and finance, and serve as the senior technical voice for the platform.

  • Serve as an escalation point for major incidents, and drive organization-wide improvements to incident management, reliability targets, and disaster recovery.

  • Lead cost, capacity, and efficiency strategy for our cloud footprint, with measurable goals.

  • Drive adoption of automation and AI-assisted operations to reduce toil across the organization.

  • Mentor Staff and Senior engineers, raise the bar on design review and engineering practice, and help us hire and develop the next generation of infrastructure leaders.

jobs.title: Product Manager (Outbound) - Identity
jobs.description_html:
About the Role

Abnormal AI is seeking a Product Manager (Outbound) to drive our next chapter in Identity. Our existing Account Takeover Protection module is established and widely adopted, and we are now expanding that footprint via Identity Threat Protection. This role will own the field motion for both products as we build toward a more cohesive, unified security experience for our customers.

Outbound Product Management (OPM) is R&D's operating layer in the field, the function that sits between what we build and how it performs with customers. That means running structured validation before a playbook exists, testing messaging in live customer conversations, and distinguishing a real product gap from a positioning or sales-motion gap. You'll work in close partnership with Product Management and Product Marketing—OPM owns the field motion, not the roadmap, but the pattern analysis and positioning work you bring back is what keeps both teams calibrated to what's actually happening with customers.

This is not a feedback-intake role. You'll validate that a pattern holds across accounts rather than resting on a single anecdote, and know when a read is solid enough to bring back to the cross-functional team versus when it needs more digging. Your identity background is what makes this work: you'll earn the trust of a customer's security team by going deep on IAM, authentication, and access patterns, and translate what you hear into something Product and Product Marketing can act on.

What You'll Do

Near-term 

  • Own the field motion for Identity Threat Protection: demos, deep dives, and POVs with prospective and existing customers.
  • Test and refine messaging hypotheses in live deals alongside Sales Engineers, and diagnose competitive loss reasons.
  • Collaborate with PM and PMM to build out a proven, repeatable field playbook, grounded in pattern analysis across accounts.

Long-term

  • Lead standing ownership of the identity product area within OPM, carrying it forward permanently as the product moves through its lifecycle.
  • Run adoption diagnostics on identity features and support technical evaluations in competitive renewals.
  • Partner with Product Marketing as a standing collaborator on identity messaging and competitive positioning as new pressures emerge and the product/competitive landscape shifts.

Must-Have Skills

  • 4+ years in Product Management or Solutions/Sales Engineering, with demonstrated depth in identity security (IAM, IGA, PAM, or SSO/authentication). This domain knowledge is a firm requirement; the learning curve in front of a customer's security team is not one we can afford.
  • Experience working in a pre-launch or early-stage product environment before a playbook existed, with a specific program, motion, or deliverable built from scratch to show for it.
  • Strong written and verbal communication; credible in front of technical buyers and security teams, equally comfortable in a live customer deep-dive and an internal roadmap review.
  • High operational excellence and ownership: you've taken a field observation from raw signal to a documented recommendation that a PM or GTM team acted on.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the capacity to reason through ambiguous problems and make effective, well-justified recommendations.

Nice to Have

  • Direct experience with account takeover (ATO), session/privilege abuse, or identity-based attack patterns specifically.
  • Prior involvement in a new-product launch, early-access program, or beta motion.
  • Experience running or presenting in structured cross-functional forums (POV reviews, launch/GTM syncs).
  • Familiarity with identity platforms such as Okta, Microsoft Entra, SailPoint, BeyondTrust, or Ping Identity.
  • Comfort using AI tools to synthesize patterns across large sets of qualitative input (support tickets, call transcripts, win/loss notes).
  • Prior startup experience.

Why This Role Matters

This role is a career inflection point. If you come from a product management background, this is where you build the GTM fluency that traditional PM roles don't give you, and that fluency is increasingly what separates good product people from exceptional ones. If you come from a solutions engineering background, this is where technical credibility becomes strategic ownership. Either way, you'll own a key product area from day one, your work will show up directly in how customers buy and adopt what we've built, and you'll come out the other side with a profile that's genuinely hard to replicate elsewhere.
