The TDI Client Platform Engineering Team

The Technology, Data, and Insights (TDI) team is on a mission to accelerate Okta’s scale. We are a group of innovative engineers who prioritize automation, testing, and performance tuning. We touch every part of the business, and we are obsessed with creating a seamless, secure end-user experience for every Okta employee.

The Staff Client Platform Engineer Opportunity

As a Staff Client Platform Engineer, you will be the subject matter expert for Okta’s macOS and iOS fleet. While your primary focus is the Apple ecosystem, you will also play a key role in our broader endpoint strategy, contributing to our Windows, Android, Linux, and VDI management workflows as needed. This is an ideal path for an engineer who wants to maintain deep Apple expertise while expanding their influence across the entire OS landscape.

We are looking for a versatile engineer who thinks automation-first. You will combine Jamf Pro expertise with open-source tools like Munki and Santa, while helping to bridge the gap between platforms using unified tools like FleetDM.

What makes this role unique: You are Customer Zero. Because we build identity and device management products, you will work directly with Okta’s own Product and Engineering teams to validate new capabilities across platforms, surface real-world feedback, and help shape the roadmap for tools used by millions of people globally.

This role reports to the Senior Manager of Client Platform Engineering.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Apple Fleet Management: Own the global macOS and iOS fleet using Jamf Pro, overseeing enrollment, configuration profiles, and application deployment.
  • Cross-Platform Support: Contribute to the management and security of Windows (via Intune/Autopilot) and Linux endpoints as the program evolves, ensuring a consistent security posture across all OS types.
  • Tooling & Evolution: Administer open-source tools (Munki, Santa) and lead evaluations of emerging platforms like FleetDM to enhance cross-platform fleet visibility.
  • Security & Compliance: Ensure endpoints meet NIST, CIS, and STIG standards. Partner with Security teams to respond to vulnerabilities across the entire fleet.
  • Engineering & Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Apply an IaC mindset to device management using code-based workflows (e.g., Terraform, Ansible, or Jamf API). Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines to ensure repeatable, scalable, and automated deployments regardless of the OS.
  • Technical Direction: Set the architecture and technical direction for a domain, such as Apple platform, endpoint security tooling or devices-as-code, and write design or docs that formalize it.
  • Customer Zero Advocacy: Act as a primary feedback loop for Okta’s internal product teams. Test new features in production and influence the product roadmap based on operational data.
  • Operational Excellence: Provide Tier 3 escalation support for global IT teams and participate in an on-call rotation.

What You’ll Bring

  • Core Experience: 8+ years in endpoint engineering with a focus on Apple platforms at enterprise scale.
  • Technical Versatility: A strong understanding of Windows and Linux operating systems; you aren't just a "Mac person", you understand how to apply engineering principles to any OS.
  • MDM Mastery: Deep expertise in managing endpoints at scale via MDM, such as Jamf Pro. Familiarity with Microsoft Intune, FleetDM or other cross-platform MDM/UEM solutions is a significant plus.
  • Scripting: Proficiency in Bash, Python, Go, or Swift (PowerShell experience is a bonus).
  • Tooling: Experience with Git, GitHub Actions, Terraform, or similar CI/CD frameworks.
  • Security: Understanding of ADE/DEP, MDM/DDM protocols, and platform-specific hardening (e.g., BitLocker, FileVault, LUKS).
  • Identity Knowledge: Familiarity with SAML and OIDC and how they integrate with endpoint authentication.

Additional requirements:

  • This position requires the ability to access federal environments and/or have access to protected federal data.  As a condition of employment for this position, the successful candidate must be able to submit documentation establishing U.S. Person status (e.g. a U.S. Citizen, National, Lawful Permanent Resident, Refugee, or Asylee. 22 CFR 120.15) upon hire.

Extra Credit

  • Hands-on experience with FleetDM or osquery for multi-OS visibility.
  • Experience with Autopkg pipelines or AWS Lambda for endpoint automation.
  • Background in Federal compliance (FedRAMP).
  • Relevant certifications (Apple, Okta, Microsoft, AWS, Jamf).

The Staff Software Engineer Opportunity

The team that built Jeeva AI is building Digital Workers, a new suite of autonomous agents for identity operations and security inside Okta. The team works directly with Todd McKinnon, Okta's co-founder and CEO, with the opportunity to bring this product to Okta's 20,000+ customers. You will help shape the product with the ownership and pace of a startup and the resources of a public company.

You will build the harnesses and evaluations that make these workers reliable. They investigate risk, use tools, wait for approvals and complete tasks across enterprise systems. Bring depth in agent execution or model quality and help turn it into working software customers can trust.

About You

Production builder: You have shipped AI software and know what changes when real users depend on it.

Careful evaluator: You investigate failures and use evidence to judge quality.

Strong owner: You follow an improvement through code, evaluation, release and customer use.

What you will be doing

  • Build the agent harness for planning, tool use, memory, context compaction, interruption and recovery during long-running work.
  • Integrate OpenAI and Anthropic model APIs. Select models using measured quality, latency and cost, with clear failure handling.
  • Evaluate existing harnesses and build only the missing pieces. Keep the harness connected to AWS workflow execution and approval state.
  • Keep authorization and sensitive writes behind application policy checks. Require evidence of the resulting state before marking work complete.
  • Build evaluation datasets and replay tests for valid findings, access decisions, app setup and AI agent onboarding.
  • Measure false positives, missed risks, unsafe actions, completion rate and cost. Turn production failures into regression tests.
  • Test prompt injection, stale evidence, conflicting instructions and unsafe tool use. Protect tenant boundaries in retrieval and memory.
  • Improve prompts, retrieval, tools and model routing. Evaluate fine-tuning or other post-training methods when results justify them and data use is approved.

What you will bring to the role

  • Strong Python engineering skills and experience shipping an LLM application that uses tools.
  • Hands-on experience building agent workflows or evaluation systems for tool-using LLM applications. For harness work, relevant experience includes Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Codex SDK, Strands Agents, LangChain Deep Agents, LangGraph or a custom implementation.
  • Experience integrating model APIs, structured outputs and asynchronous services. Experience with OpenAI or Anthropic is especially relevant.
  • Depth in agent execution or evaluation systems, with working code and failure analysis you can explain.
  • Ability to distinguish a plausible model response from a supported finding or verified action.

Scope by level

Staff: Lead a domain such as harnesses, evaluations or model quality across workers and implement its critical components.

Our stack

Our core stack is Python FastAPI, AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, PostgreSQL on Amazon RDS and pgvector. OpenAI and Anthropic model APIs are part of the integration plan.

We plan to add an agent harness and a dedicated analytics layer using ClickHouse or BigQuery. The harness choice is open. Experience with equivalent tools also counts.

And extra credit for

  • Open-source contributions, agent observability, security evaluations or synthetic evaluation data.
  • Fine-tuning, preference data, post-training evaluation or model distillation using approved datasets.
  • Identity and security workflows. Foundation-model research experience is optional.

jobs.title: Product Analyst III
jobs.description_html:
Are you looking for a role in a company that's solving one of the greatest challenges of our lifetime? Ophelia helps people end their opioid use and restore their quality of life with respect for their time and dignity. Our mission is to make evidence-based treatments for opioid use disorder (OUD) accessible to everyone... and we're looking to bring more people onto our team to help us achieve it.
 
Ophelia is a venture-backed, healthcare startup that helps individuals with OUD by providing FDA-approved medication and clinical care through a telehealth platform. Our approach is discreet, convenient, and affordable. We've been successfully operating in 16 states for almost six years and we're excited to continue our growth. We are a team of physicians, scientists, entrepreneurs, researchers and White House advisors, backed by leading technology and healthcare investors working to re-imagine and re-build OUD treatment in America.

About the Role

As a Senior Product Analyst, you will turn data into decisions that prove telehealth to be the best way to treat opioid use disorder! You will be the go-to analytical partner for all three of our product squads, shaping how we measure success, designing and reading out experiments, and helping our teams understand what patients truly need. You will work cross-functionally with product managers, engineers, product designers, clinicians, operators, marketers, billers, and more (this role is perfect if you want to fully immerse in technology-enabled healthcare services). You are right for this role if your statistics tools are razor-sharp and you enjoy  immersing yourself in experiment construction and analyses. Together, you will frame the right questions, test ideas quickly, and learn in an iterative way. Ultimately, you will make sure our product decisions are grounded in rigorous evidence, centered on patients, and connected to Ophelia's goals.

To date, we have built a portfolio of bespoke patient and clinical applications, bespoke billing and clinical data services, and commercial integrations, all of which have been core to achieving our goals. Looking forward, our technology roadmap is rich with innovative opportunities across paid-digital, B2B, and peer-led growth, new clinical services, applications of AI for clinicians and Care Coordinators, and a whole lot more. Every one of these bets needs strong measurement and smart experiments, and that is where you come in. Together, we will build awesome products while we embark towards profitability, our next milestone.

Our Technology team today is small but mighty and works in close collaboration across software engineering, product design, product management, and data. We use an agile approach rooted in the principles of the Agile Manifesto and are growing a strong experiment culture across our squads. Our product suite includes a custom-built EMR platform for our clinical organization and a patient portal, alongside numerous interaction modes (including text messaging, video conferencing, and third-party software). Our analytics stack includes BigQuery, Lightdash, FullStory, and LaunchDarkly, and we work in SQL, Python, and R.

In this fully remote role, you will report to Becca Getto, our Manager of Product Management, and support all three of our product squads, working across Technology broadly. You will also partner closely with our Data team through our Data Council, including our Data Analysts and Analytics Engineers. Together, we'll help hard-to-reach people treat their opioid dependence. You may not have experience in this treatment area, but ideally, you'll have knowledge of the healthcare space, including understanding health outcomes and benchmarks, systems, and regulatory compliance (HIPAA).

Responsibilities

  • Lead experimentation across our product squads, partnering with product managers, engineering, and product design to shape hypotheses, size and design tests, monitor them in flight, and deliver clear readouts. Help grow a culture where every team loves to test and learn.
  • Design and maintain our product metrics, including success metrics, guardrails, and leading indicators for each squad. Validate metric health, build trusted dashboards in Lightdash, and make sure teams can track what matters.
  • Deliver deep-dive analyses on patient and clinician behavior, including funnels, engagement, retention, and outcomes. When a randomized test isn't possible, use quasi-experimental methods to get to the best available answer.
  • Study and share outcomes and learnings with squad teams, our leadership team, and in large format meetings. Turn complex analyses into clear stories and recommendations that drive action.
  • Ensure a patient-centered focus by pairing quantitative analysis with qualitative signals such as FullStory sessions, user research, and feedback, so the numbers always connect back to real people.
  • Partner with the Data Council and our Data Analysts and Analytics Engineers to improve instrumentation, data quality, shared definitions, and analytics tooling.
  • Stay current with industry trends, emerging methods, and best practices in product analytics and experimentation. Network frequently beyond Ophelia and share learnings with the team.

Skills & Competencies

  • 4+ years experience in product analytics for consumer-oriented digital products, with a track record of driving stellar business outcomes through experimentation and insight. Demonstrate strong business acumen to connect analyses to strategy, keep track of key metrics and KPIs, and help teams prioritize the work that matters most.
  • Excellent statistics with deep, hands-on command of experimentation methods, including sample size and power calculations (MDE), variance reduction (e.g., CUPED), sequential and Bayesian approaches, and correcting for common pitfalls such as sample ratio mismatch, novelty effects, and multiple testing. Comfortable choosing the right parametric or non-parametric test, working with ratio metrics, and applying causal inference methods such as diff-in-diff, propensity score matching, regression discontinuity, and synthetic controls.
  • Experiment culture builder who loves helping teams form strong hypotheses, design tight tests, and ship early iterations to learn quickly. You make experimentation easier and more trusted for everyone around you.
  • Strong technical fluency in SQL and Python or R, with experience in cloud data warehouses such as BigQuery. Experience with BI tools (we use Lightdash), session and behavior analytics (we use FullStory), and feature flagging (we use LaunchDarkly) is a plus. Experience in tools like Mixpanel or Amplitude is also relevant.
  • Customer- and patient-oriented business mindset, with the ability to translate data into a clear understanding of what our patients and clinicians need, and what it means for the business.
  • Stellar communications and data storytelling, comfortable presenting analyses to groups of all sizes, from squad teams to leadership to large format meetings. You create strong points of view, backed with data, and tailor the message to your audience.
  • Impact orientation with focus on delivering outcomes over outputs, choosing to work in a thoughtful, iterative way. You capture learnings, share them broadly, and apply them to future decisions.
  • Passionate about our mission to make evidence-based addiction treatment universally accessible. Any experience in healthcare or telehealth is a nice plus!

jobs.title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer (Systems Engineer III)
jobs.description_html:
Are you looking for a role in a company that's solving one of the greatest challenges of our lifetime? Ophelia helps people end their opioid use and restore their quality of life with respect for their time and dignity. Our mission is to make evidence-based treatments for opioid use disorder (OUD) accessible to everyone... and we're looking to bring more people onto our team to help us achieve it.
 
Ophelia is a venture-backed, healthcare startup that helps individuals with OUD by providing FDA-approved medication and clinical care through a telehealth platform. Our approach is discreet, convenient, and affordable. We've been successfully operating in 16 states for almost six years and we're excited to continue our growth. We are a team of physicians, scientists, entrepreneurs, researchers and White House advisors, backed by leading technology and healthcare investors working to re-imagine and re-build OUD treatment in America.

About the Role

As a Senior Site Reliability Engineer (SE III) at Ophelia, you will be our dedicated reliability, availability, and performance hire, playing a key role in making the systems that support our mission of treating opioid use disorder through telehealth stable, observable, and fast. Our stack is TypeScript on Node, React, and Firebase (e.g., Firestore, Authentication, Hosting) running on Cloud Run in Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Your work will have a direct impact on patients, clinicians, and our ability to scale.

You will own and drive our system stability and availability initiative, which is already underway: Terraform-driven uptime checks feed our engineering key performance indicators (KPIs), we have an initial service level objective (SLO) plan, and we've recently revamped our on-call rotation and runbook to keep the on-call engineer focused on severity incidents (SEVs). You will take this from a good start to a mature practice: defining and operationalizing SLOs, building out logging, monitoring, and alerting grounded in sound measurement (e.g., percentile-based latency indicators rather than averages), moving incident response into PagerDuty with clear categorization and escalation paths, expanding our infrastructure as code (IaC) footprint, and working down known pain points such as long-latency endpoints and Cloud Run cold starts. You will also partner closely with our head of IT on IAM hardening, secrets management, audit logging, and HIPAA/SOC 2 infrastructure controls. You will be the directly responsible individual (DRI) for our mean time to recovery (MTTR) KPI and for the measurement and reporting of our availability KPIs.

As a senior engineer, you will be a force multiplier for our team of fullstack engineers who are focused on product work. That means leveling up the team's GCP and DevOps skills through documentation, runbooks, pairing, and code review, and bringing reliability recommendations to new features as they are designed, while primarily owning the infrastructure work yourself. This role is entirely reliability-focused for the first six months; after that, you may contribute to product work as needed, though product work will be at most about 25% of your time.

Ophelia's Technology team actively encourages and invests in AI-augmented ways of working: using tools like Claude and Gemini to accelerate infrastructure code, runbooks, log analysis, and incident triage, and staying current as the AI landscape evolves. Consistent with Ophelia's AI Position Statement, we treat AI as a force multiplier for our team, not a replacement for human judgment: it's there to help you move faster from alert to root cause and spend more time on the reliability and architecture decisions that actually require a person. You'll be expected to use AI fluently in your own workflow, to build it into our operational tooling, and to help shape how the larger technology team uses it responsibly and effectively as it evolves.

Together, we will help hard-to-reach individuals treat their opioid dependence. While direct experience in this treatment area is not mandatory, knowledge of the healthcare space, including understanding health outcomes, benchmarks, systems, and regulatory compliance (HIPAA), is highly beneficial.

Responsibilities

  • Own reliability, availability, and performance of our GCP platform. Define and operationalize SLOs and service level indicators (SLIs) with the team, and drive the work that moves them (e.g., endpoint latency, Cloud Run cold starts, time to recovery), and own our disaster recovery posture (e.g., Firestore backup and restore testing, recovery point and recovery time objectives, and multi-region resilience).
  • Build observability and incident response. Extend our GCP Cloud Operations setup (log-based metrics, alerting policies, dashboards), move alerting from Slack into PagerDuty, participate in our on-call rotation alongside the rest of the team, and mature that process with clear incident categorization, escalation paths, and an AI-assisted level-one triage tool.
  • Grow our infrastructure as code and delivery pipeline. Expand our Terraform footprint beyond observability metrics and ephemeral pull request (PR) environments to the rest of our GCP configuration, and improve our GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline so that deploying four times a day gets safer and faster, not riskier.
  • Harden security and compliance controls in partnership with our head of IT, who is the DRI for IT security and our HIPAA/SOC 2 infrastructure controls.
  • Multiply the team. Level up our engineers' GCP and DevOps skills through presentations, docs, runbooks, pairing, and code review; bring reliability recommendations to new features early; share reusable AI skills and automation across the team; and set the bar for operational excellence by embodying Ophelia's core values.
  • Take ownership of your work in our remote, growth-stage environment, driving projects from inception to impact with autonomy and proactive communication, adapting as our priorities evolve, and staying current with industry practice (including AI tooling) in reliability and cloud infrastructure.

Skills & Competencies

  • 5+ years experience in engineering, including 3+ in a cloud infrastructure, DevOps, or SRE-focused role, ideally with a portion at a growth-stage company with bespoke systems.
  • Expert-level, hands-on GCP fluency, including serverless compute (e.g., Cloud Run), Cloud Operations (Logging, Monitoring, alerting), IAM, and Firebase/Firestore. Terraform fluency is strongly preferred.
  • Expert in at least one language used for infrastructure automation (e.g., Python) and strong in shell scripting. You should be comfortable reading and debugging TypeScript/Node, as that's our entire application codebase; SQL for BigQuery and Log Analytics is a plus.
  • Production operations experience, including participating in on-call, leading incident response, writing postmortems, and defining SLOs in keeping with Google SRE practice, and the judgment to adapt those practices to a small team's capacity rather than importing large-company process wholesale.
  • Quantitative fluency applied to production systems, e.g., percentiles and tail latency rather than averages, SLO and error-budget math, burn-rate alerting, and reading time series and histograms well enough to tell signal from noise.
  • Senior-level ownership and communication, with the ability to own complex, ambiguous projects end-to-end with technical and non-technical stakeholders, clear and proactive communication, and a habit of writing things down (runbooks, postmortems, design docs) and pairing so that knowledge doesn't live only with you.
  • Daily, hands-on use of AI tools in your own engineering work (e.g., Claude Code for Terraform, runbooks, and log analysis), and experience building automation with them rather than only using them.

Preferred

  • Passionate about our mission to make evidence-based addiction treatment universally accessible.
  • Background in a regulated industry, ideally healthcare - telehealth is a big plus - with hands-on experience implementing HIPAA or SOC 2 infrastructure controls.

Our Benefits Include

  • Competitive medical, vision, and health insurance (many plans are fully covered for the employee!)
  • Start with 20 days (4 weeks) of PTO, increasing to 5 weeks after 2 years and 6 weeks after 5 years of tenure
  • 10 company holidays
  • Work From Home Stipend
  • 401k Contribution Platform
  • Additional benefits offered through our benefits provider such as life insurance, short and long term disability, financial wellness, virtual primary care, among others!

Ophelia Compensation Overview
  • We set compensation based on the level and skills required for the role. We value pay transparency and equity, and are committed to fair pay. In order to prevent pay disparities and reduce time spent in negotiations, we take a “first and best” offer approach: this means we’re not holding any compensation back from our candidates, and you can feel confident that our pay is fair and does not vary based on the strength of someone’s negotiation skills.

When a feature needs changes in other parts of our system you will often jump in and help implement those. This is a high-impact, high-autonomy role where you’ll shape real-time geospatial UIs that integrate live video, maps, and controls for complex defense systems. You will work closely with product, design, and customers to turn ambiguous needs into shipping products at lightning speed. jobs.title: Product Designer
jobs.description_html:
About Primer

Primer is a growing network of K–8 schools restoring the timeless foundations of American education. Inspired by the original teaching primers that shaped a nation of readers, thinkers, and builders, our schools begin with what has always worked, and build for what lies ahead. Close-knit learning environments. Skilled educators. A culture that takes kids seriously as learners and leaders.

Primers shaped the first 200 years of American children. Primer will ready them for the next.

About the role

You’ll own the end-to-end design for the experiences that make Primer schools great. That includes web and mobile products for families, students, educators, and internal teams, as well as the physical campuses themselves. From the app parents use every day, to the signage they see when they walk into a school, you’ll help us define it all.

 

Most edtech companies stop at software. We run the schools, source the real estate, hire the teachers, and build the spaces where learning happens. The same person who designs the digital onboarding flow also has a point of view on how the classroom flows.

 

You’ll join a small, high-ownership design team that works close to students, families, educators, and operators. We value clear thinking, honest feedback, strong craft, and a bias toward action.

 

You’ll work closely with product, engineering, and school operators to solve problems that have never been solved before. The goal is to build simple, intuitive, and joyful experiences for all our users and scale our products for our next phase of growth.

What you’ll do:

  • Lead design projects from initial concept through high-fidelity design and launch.

  • Run user research with students, families, and teachers, and turn what you learn into interfaces, systems, and environments.

  • Move fluidly between visual design, interaction design, and systems thinking depending on what the product needs.

  • Refine copy, tone, and visual detail so every screen feels cohesive and intentional.

  • Contribute to and help shape the Mondrian design system.

  • Design beyond the screen: campus signage, interior spaces and marketing assets

  • Help set Primer's design standards and raise the ceiling of the team as it grows.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years of experience as Product Designer

  • An exceptionally polished portfolio

  • A track record of owning projects end-to-end, from concept through launch.

  • A strong sense of language and consistency

  • Comfort balancing insight with intuition. You can commit to a direction without waiting for formal research to hand you the answer.

  • Strength bringing clarity to big, ambiguous problem spaces

  • Comfortable presenting to executives, board members, investors and non-tech stakeholders

  • Experience using AI tools to prototype and convey designs is a plus

  • High EQ. You work well with people who aren't designers, take feedback in a room full of them, and can read what students, families, and teachers actually need.

  • Genuine excitement about Primer's mission

  • This is a full-time, in-person role based in San Francisco, as we believe our best work happens when we’re together.

Something Extra: We value diverse backgrounds — whether in education, healthcare, logistics, marketplaces, compliance, field operations, or something entirely different. Anything that taught you how complex human systems really work.

 

Why Join Primer

We're building something really hard — a new school system. The product challenges are incredibly varied and you'll use every skill in your toolkit. Watch our CEO Ryan talk about the inspiration, the challenges, and the impact we’re having in this interview.

 

As a fast-growing startup, we offer salary commensurate with experience, plus significant equity and comprehensive benefits including 100% health insurance, life insurance, and daily lunch.

Primer is a mission-first company. We believe our mission is the highest-leverage way we can create positive change. jobs.title: Product Manager, Mission Planning
jobs.description_html:
Product Manager, Mission Planning

We’re looking for a technically minded Product Manager to join our growing team and lead the evolution of Quindar’s Mission Planning capabilities across our Plan and Portal products.

Quindar provides a unified platform to automate and accelerate mission operations. Our customers operate constellations with different missions, architectures, operational constraints, and levels of autonomy. Mission Planning sits at the intersection of those needs: helping operators understand what needs to happen, when it can happen, what constraints apply, and how plans ultimately become operational activities.

In this role, you’ll own how missions translate operational objectives into executable plans, from scheduling spacecraft activities and ground contacts to coordinating requests between mission teams, payload operators, and other stakeholders. You’ll help make increasingly complex mission operations easier to plan, coordinate, and automate as our customers scale from individual spacecraft to large, diverse fleets.

You’ll own key parts of the product lifecycle — from discovery and prioritization to launch and iteration — working closely with engineering, design, customer-facing teams, and other Product Managers. You should be comfortable diving into scheduling logic, operational constraints, mission workflows, and system architecture while keeping user empathy and product clarity at the center of your decisions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Strategy & Vision: Own the roadmap and long-term vision for Mission Planning across Quindar’s Plan and Portal products. Define product requirements, user stories, success metrics, and priorities that align customer needs with Quindar’s broader mission operations strategy.

  • Execution: Collaborate closely with engineering and design to turn operational problems into intuitive, scalable product capabilities. Participate in technical and architecture discussions and make thoughtful tradeoffs between immediate customer needs, usability, and long-term product health.

  • User Understanding: Develop deep empathy for mission operators, payload operators, mission planners, and other users by conducting research, shadowing workflows, analyzing operational data, and synthesizing feedback from customer-facing teams.

  • Automation & Scale: Identify opportunities to move customers from manual planning and coordination toward increasingly automated and constraint-aware workflows. Ensure planning capabilities can scale from individual spacecraft to large fleets and increasingly complex mission architectures.

  • Planning & Scheduling: Evolve how operators plan spacecraft activities, ground contacts, payload operations, and other mission activities. Develop capabilities that account for operational constraints, resource availability, dependencies, priorities, and changing mission conditions.

  • Multi-Party Mission Operations: Define workflows that enable mission operators, payload operators, customers, and other stakeholders to coordinate effectively while maintaining appropriate operational boundaries and permissions. Make it easy for users to request activities, understand their status, and maintain situational awareness without requiring direct control of the spacecraft.

  • Metrics & Iteration: Define and track measures of planning effectiveness, including planning time, scheduling success, operator intervention, request turnaround, utilization, and adoption of automated workflows. Use data and customer feedback to continuously improve the product.

  • Leadership: Serve as the go-to expert on mission planning workflows, scheduling, payload operations, and the relevant competitive landscape. Develop a strong point of view on how mission planning should evolve as satellite operations become more distributed and autonomous.

  • Collaboration: Drive alignment across engineering, product management, design, customer success, program teams, and leadership. Clearly communicate priorities, dependencies, and tradeoffs across technical and non-technical stakeholders.

What Makes This Role Unique

  • You’ll shape how complex spacecraft operations move from mission objectives to executable plans.

  • You’ll design workflows for an increasingly diverse set of operators — from teams directly commanding spacecraft to payload customers who need awareness and access without owning the spacecraft bus.

  • You’ll tackle planning problems involving real operational constraints, limited resources, competing priorities, and dynamic mission conditions.

  • You’ll help customers transition from manual scheduling and coordination toward increasingly automated mission planning.

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years of product management experience, preferably in aerospace, schedule optimization, autonomous vehicle operations, or complex technical SaaS products.

  • Proven ability to own product roadmaps and deliver complex features end-to-end.

  • Ability to obtain a U.S. Security Clearance required.

  • Demonstrated ability to understand complex user workflows and translate them into intuitive product experiences.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, cross-functional leadership, and prioritization skills.

  • Bachelor’s degree in geospatial, computer science, aerospace, business, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

  • Ability to excel in a fast-paced, evolving environment with high ownership.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with satellite mission planning, spacecraft operations, ground segment systems, or aerospace scheduling.

  • Experience designing products for multiple user personas with different roles, permissions, and levels of operational authority.

  • Active U.S. Security Clearance (Secret or higher) preferred

Technical Recruiter

Help hire the people building the infrastructure for space.

At Quindar, we’re making it possible to operate satellites like servers. This role calls for someone who brings urgency, resourcefulness, and strong relationship skills. You should be comfortable reaching passive candidates, learning the details of unfamiliar technical roles, and turning a first conversation into a successful hire.

jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer, Agentic Systems
jobs.description_html:
About the team:

Rubrik secures and accelerates the world’s AI transformation. As AI agents reshape the enterprise, Rubrik’s Enterprise AI Incubation team proves it on Rubrik itself.
We are building a thinking enterprise: applications that don't just record the business but help run it. They learn from our data, act through our own agents, and improve with every decision.
Fully backed by executive leadership, this team drives meaningful, large-scale enterprise transformation.

About the role:

We want senior engineers who have already shipped agents that real people rely on, and who are ready to do it again at higher stakes. You will drop into the real work, redesign it around agents that carry it end to end, and ship it as the new way that part of Rubrik operates.You’ll own your agent systems end to end: understanding the workflow, designing the architecture, writing the code, deploying, and running it in production. Rather than simply querying an API, you engineer robust, production-grade infrastructure around model endpoints, integrating custom tooling, context pipelines, automated evaluations, and defensive guardrails to ensure resilience against unstructured real-world data.

You also decide whether a problem needs an agent, a simpler automation, or nothing at all, and you have explicit authority to stop or re-scope work that won’t deliver impact. You thrive in ambiguous environments with a low-ego mindset, leveraging AI coding tools as core collaborative partners in your engineering workflow.

What you’ll do:

  • Lead product discovery alongside Product Managers and domain experts to understand real workflows, map them out, and define clear problems, baselines, and success criteria as the foundation for building agentic solutions.
  • Design, build, test, and deploy production agents, automations, and internal tools using coding agents, LLM APIs, and agent frameworks, integrated with Rubrik’s internal agent platform and business systems.
  • Turn complex processes into multi-agent workflows that carry real work and make decisions: orchestrators that qualify and routes deals, workers that move orders through approval and fulfillment under business rules, agents that monitor signals and recommend actions for customer health, or coordinated agents that handle hire-to-retire steps across HR, IT, and managers with shared state and clear handoffs.
  • Engineer agents for autonomy with reliability, including tool and orchestration flows, context management, caching, retries, and failure handling.
  • Leverage full-stack engineering across backend services, APIs, data models, interactive screens, approval UIs, and chat interfaces as the complete medium to deliver high-ownership, user-facing agent systems.
  • Apply solid software engineering practices to AI systems, treating prompts, skills, configs, and specs as versioned artifacts, with code review, tests, CI or CD, and staged rollouts.
  • Implement evaluation, guardrails, and quality control: derive evals from workflow data, establish quality gates and guardrails, integrate human-in-the-loop approvals where needed, and monitor production runs to refine agents over time.
  • Use measured results to decide how to evolve or retire agents, and turn successful systems into patterns and libraries that can be reused.

Experience you’ll need:

  • Around 7 or more years of professional software engineering experience in production systems, and around 2 or more years of professional, hands-on experience building AI agents and agent powered production applications with measurable outcomes.
  • Strong full stack engineering background, with a track record of designing, building, and owning services end to end, including backend APIs and integrations, data models, and user facing interfaces such as approval UIs, dashboards, or chat surfaces.
  • A builder mindset: comfortable defining baselines and metrics, reporting results in business terms, working in a fast moving environment, and closing the loop by building, demoing, learning, and building again. If you like seeing improvements in hours saved, errors avoided, and teams unblocked, you will have plenty of chances to measure that here.

Software engineering skills and best practices:

  • System design: break down complex problems, design APIs and data models, reason about latency, throughput, and failure modes, and choose simple, robust architectures.
  • Algorithms, data structures, access control permissions, and data provenance.
  • Spec driven development: turn vague requirements into clear problem statements, write or refine design docs, and use a Spec → Plan → Task → Code→ Converge flow so work is traceable from design to code, including when you use AI coding agents.
  • Execution discipline: use version control, code review, automated tests, CI or CD, staged rollouts and rollbacks, logging, metrics, and tracing, and improve systems based on issues and signals from production.

AI engineering skills and best practices:

  • Build agents in code using LLM APIs, SDKs, and libraries, not just no code or low code tools, and have shipped agentic systems that real users rely on.
  • Design robust agent harnesses and multi agent orchestrations: model tools and resources, manage context and state, and keep runs reliable under real world data and load.
  • Establish continuous evaluation and safety mechanisms: turn production failures into test cases, gate changes on eval suite results, and enforce guardrails across agent workflows.
  • Exercise clear judgment on AI fit: decide when a problem needs an agent versus a simpler automation or no build, and make tradeoffs around model choice, latency and cost, context strategy, and autonomy using data rather than intuition.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Knowledge/context graphs: entities and relationships, GraphRAG, hybrid retrieval.
  • Agent frameworks and runtimes: Google ADK, LangGraph, OpenAI style, cloud or container platforms.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI or similar stacks.
  • Tools integration: MCP, Slack or Teams bots, REST APIs, webhooks.
  • Data systems: Snowflake, Salesforce, graph stores.
  • UX: conversational flows, chat surfaces, guided forms, simple dashboards for agent output.

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description_html:
About the Team & Role:

We're building SAGE, Rubrik's Semantic AI Governance Engine, which is the first system designed to monitor, govern, and remediate autonomous AI agents in real time. SAGE powers Rubrik Agent Cloud: enterprises define governance policies in natural language, and SAGE's custom small language models act as judges on every agent action. These models are fast enough to sit in the live request path and accurate enough that customers trust them with allow/block decisions on production traffic.

At its core, SAGE is "LLM-as-judge" applied to AI governance, utilizing the same technique most teams use for offline evaluation but productionized for real-time enforcement at enterprise scale. Our first-generation SLM Policy Guard already outperforms the larger frontier models we've benchmarked against on accuracy while running approximately 5x faster on the same workload. We're hiring to push that lead even further.

As an Applied ML Engineer on the SAGE team, you'll work end-to-end across the model lifecycle: curating data, training small models, serving them at production latency, and closing the feedback loop with real customer signals. The models you build don't just enforce policies in the live request path; they will also drive Agent Rewind, Rubrik's capability to instantly and precisely undo destructive autonomous-agent actions and restore the affected data to a trusted state. 

We're a collaborative, applied team that ships models to enterprise customers within weeks, and we're passionate about proving that small, specialized models can outperform frontier LLMs at the problems that matter most for AI safety and governance.

Nature of the Specialized Duties

➢ Training, Fine-Tuning, and Distilling Production Small Language Models and Classifiers (25% of time)

  • Owning the full training lifecycle for the SLMs and classifiers in SAGE's real-time enforcement path, including base-model selection, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization (DPO/RLAIF), and distillation from frontier teacher models.
  • Training anomaly and action-severity models that catch novel agent-side attack patterns at real-time decision latency, such as supply-chain compromises or emergent destructive behaviors not covered by any explicit policy. Severity scores route the highest-impact events to Agent Rewind for precise remediation.
  • Designing adversarial training pipelines like purpose-built adversarial agents and automated red-teams whose outputs feed directly into the next training run, turning every discovered weakness into a permanent model improvement.
  • Pushing the pareto frontier of accuracy, latency, and cost for governance-specific tasks through deliberate post-training choices (LoRA, quantization-aware training, distillation recipes, GRPO, etc.) and validating the wins on production traffic patterns.

➢ Engineering High-Performance Model Serving and Inference Infrastructure (25% of time)

  • Designing multi-stage inference pipelines that handle both real-time enforcement (inline prompt, response, and tool-call blocking) and high-throughput batch workloads (offline scoring, back-testing, corpus mining) while processing billions of tokens daily across Global 2000 customer agent fleets.
  • Optimizing live deployments through shared GPU pools, KV-cache-aware routing, continuous batching, FP8/INT8 quantization, and speculative decoding to minimize inference cost while holding sub-second P99 SLOs.
  • Building serving-layer infrastructure that lets SAGE block agent prompts, responses, and tool calls in real time without becoming a latency bottleneck. This includes model gateway design, request routing, and graceful degradation.
  • Owning canary, shadow, and A/B traffic patterns so new model variants are validated against live customer traffic before they take enforcement decisions.

➢ Building Synthetic Data Pipelines and Online + Offline Evaluation Frameworks (20% of time)

  • Designing automated data curation pipelines that mine live customer environments (with privacy and tenancy guarantees) for high-value per tenant training examples, such as long-tail violations, near-miss policy edges, or novel agent behaviors, and routing them back into the training loop for each customer.
  • Building automated policy back-testing by replaying historical agent traffic against new model and policy versions to catch regressions and recommend policy improvements before customer-visible deployment.
  • Building online evaluation systems for live model decisions, including shadow scoring, drift detection, calibration monitoring, and policy-coverage gap analysis, ensuring quality regressions surface in minutes rather than weeks.
  • Generating synthetic data using frontier teachers (adversarial prompts, policy-edge cases, multi-turn interactions) with evaluation that confirms synthetic data improves downstream quality, not just dataset size.

➢ Insights Mining, Failure Diagnosis, and Adaptive Model Improvement (15% of time)

  • Building memory and context harnesses that fuse data sensitivity, identity, and historical agent behavior into real-time enforcement decisions to ensure SAGE reasons from each customer's specific context.
  • Mining agent insights across millions of sessions to surface security gaps, which are then turned into new policy proposals, refinements to existing policies, and signals about upstream issues across the agent ecosystem (Google ADK, Azure AI Foundry, Vertex AI, and others).
  • Building feedback loops that turn production decisions, customer-flagged false positives, and missed violations into one-click natural-language policy refinements to drive false-positive rates down without sacrificing recall.
  • Diagnosing model failures end-to-end and distinguishing data, training-recipe, architecture, and serving-layer root causes so fixes land in the right layer the first time.

➢  Cross-Functional Collaboration and Translating Customer Reality into Modeling Problems (15% of time)

  • Providing technical leadership on a pillar of the SAGE model stack (training infrastructure, eval methodology, serving architecture, or insights pipeline), mentoring engineers ramping into ML, and shaping the team's technical roadmap.
  • Partnering with Product Management, customer-facing teams, and security analysts to translate customer agent-governance requirements into well-scoped modeling problems, and pushing back when ML is the wrong tool.
  • Communicating model behavior, tradeoffs, and limitations clearly to non-ML stakeholders, such as product managers and enterprise security leaders, so model decisions are made with full context.
  • Collaborating with Agent Cloud platform, security engineering, and AI research teams to integrate new SLMs into the real-time enforcement path with the right latency, observability, rollback, and tenancy guarantees.

Minimum Requirements for the Position

Education: A Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Computer Engineering, Statistics, or a closely related technical field is required. Designing production SLM training and serving systems requires a deep theoretical understanding of modern deep learning, optimization, and systems performance.

Specialized Technical Knowledge:

  • 2+ years of professional ML experience with demonstrable end-to-end production ownership; you have taken models from training to serving real customer traffic and stayed accountable for them through post-launch iteration.
  • Proficiency in Python and PyTorch (or equivalent) for production-grade training and evaluation.
  • Hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, or distilling language models or classifiers in a production setting, including SFT and at least one preference-optimization  technique (DPO, RLAIF, or RLHF).
  • Production experience with serving frameworks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or equivalent), including optimization involving continuous batching, KV-cache strategy, and inference-time quantization.
  • Experience designing closed-loop ML systems, including the eval, telemetry, data-curation, and synthetic-data infrastructure that turns production signals back into training data and the next model release. You have built (not just used) at least one such loop.
  • Comfort operating at production scale, including debugging models that handle high QPS in safety-critical request paths where errors have customer-visible consequences.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Deep background in AI safety and red-teaming, including hands-on experience with adversarial ML, prompt injection defense strategies, and automated evaluation suites for enterprise-grade LLM safety.
  • Expertise in model evaluation methodology, specifically building "LLM-as-judge" pipelines, calibration monitoring, and adversarial benchmarks that surface the subtle failure modes static metrics often overlook.
  • Experience with context-fusion and retrieval systems that synthesize disparate signals - such as data sensitivity, user identity, and behavioral history - into high-fidelity model decisions.
  • Production experience with low-latency inference for streaming or safety-critical request paths where model throughput and P99 SLOs are paramount.
  • Mastery of label-efficient training and data mining, utilizing weak supervision, active learning, and embedding-based retrieval to surface the production examples that drive the most significant quality improvements.
  • Hands-on knowledge distillation experience, successfully transferring capabilities from frontier teacher models to specialized, small-scale student models for production serving.
  • Familiarity with the agentic ecosystem, including tool-use frameworks, model gateway architectures (MCP, LiteLLM, or equivalent), and autonomous agent patterns.
  • Active open-source contributions to mainstream ML training, serving, or evaluation libraries.

Senior Product Manager, Control Plane (RSC-G & Government)

Location: US HQ (Hybrid) or Washington DC metro (remote)

About Rubrik

Rubrik is one of the fastest-growing companies in cyber security, revolutionizing data protection and management in the emerging multi-cloud world. We are a one-of-a-kind company with a one-of-a-kind purpose, inspiring passion and drive in team members around a meaningful purpose of securing the world's data. What we do truly matters and our team members have unlimited potential and endless possibilities for growth. We provide you with the tools, resources, and mentorship you need to develop your skills and reach new career heights. Unleash your full potential and make a lasting impact on the world.

About the Product Management Team

The Product Management team at Rubrik drives forward our vision, ensuring we continue to deliver on our market-leading platform as we address our customers' most challenging data management and security needs. Our mission is to deliver the best application-aware backups, helping customers secure their data, while ensuring that we do not compromise on the end-to-end user experience we are known for.

About the Role

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to join the Rubrik Security Cloud Control Plane team and own the product roadmap Rubrik Security Cloud-Government (RSC-G) and government-focused product initiatives across our product portfolio.

You will work with our field team and directly with customers to develop a strong, informed point of view on the prioritization for RSC-G and own the outcome. Staff Platform Product Manager,  Cloud Security Architecture

Location: Remote, USA

The Staff Product Manager for Cloud Security Architecture is a strategic role responsible for ensuring that Rubrik's cloud product offerings meet enterprise expectations for security and are secured from cyber-attacks. This technical role combines deep security expertise with strong product instincts and competitor awareness to translate customers' security challenges and concerns into actionable product requirements for Rubrik’s cloud product and cloud platform security roadmap. 

Our product stands on a foundation of "Zero Trust" security and this role is critical in driving the long-term security vision and roadmap with a  focus on identifying product gaps, market opportunities, developing long-term strategic plans, and implementing enhancements that drive industry-leading security standards and best practices into Rubrik products.

Specific Responsibilities:

  • Works closely with cloud product and engineering teams to develop a deep understanding of the Rubrik cloud product architecture
    1. Ability to articulate and defend our architectural decisions cross functionally and to customers.  
    2. Contribute to cloud product and cloud platform  security roadmap and execute for multiple, related security domains within the Rubrik offering, ensuring alignment and coherence across the portfolio.
    3. Scan and keep abreast ofcustomer expectations and evolving hyperscaler best practices.
  • Act as a primary evangelist for the cloud product security and work with customers and account teams to define and evolve the roadmap across multiple dimensions (UX, technology, business) and deliver commercially viable security features and integrations across the Rubrik cloud portfolio
  • Lead cross-functional strategic initiatives and manage the execution across all cloud products, ensuring they meet platform security standards.
  • Lead and develop product risk identification, assessment, and resolution prioritization for high-impact platform vulnerabilities.
  • Partner with and influence senior cross-functional stakeholders—including InfoSec, Engineering, User Experience, Sales, Marketing, Operations, and Support—to align vision across business units and secure project approval and resources.
  • Communicate concisely and clearly to diverse audiences, including presenting compelling business cases to executive leadership and representing Rubrik as a security expert to external audiences, customers, and ecosystem partners.
  • Drive significant business impact by identifying market opportunities and leading new product developments that contribute measurable increases to quarterly revenue, profitability, and customer trust.
  • Act as a mentor and role model for other Product Managers, sharing best practices, driving clarity in the face of ambiguity cross-functionally, and fostering strong partnerships with engineering teams.

Required Skills:

  • Experience or desire to be in Product Management, with at least 3 years focused on enterprise cloud product development with hyperscalers, ideally in a hands-on technical or architecture role.
  • Prior experience as a Security Architect, Solutions Architect, or Senior/Staff Engineer is highly desirable
  • Expertise in cloud security and threat modeling and working knowledge of big 3 hyperscalers with specific experience in cloud security posture management or secure cloud integration and defining secure architectures for solutions built on hyperscaler infrastructure.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Databases
jobs.description_html:
Staff Product Manager, Databases

Location: US - Remote

About Us

Rubrik (NYSE: RBRK) is the Security and AI Operations Company, delivering one platform built at the intersection of data, identity, and AI. The platform enables agentic cyber resilience and trusted AI operations for enterprises worldwide, built to recover before disruption strikes and stay a step ahead, so security is never the reason ambition stalls.

About the Product Management Team

At Rubrik, our Product Management team is at the forefront of defining the strategy and driving execution to strengthen our leading platform for cyber-resilience. We are dedicated to meeting the ever-changing data management and security needs of our customers and wear multiple hats throughout the different stages in the product lifecycle and set the vision for our growing family of products. As advocates for both our users and our business, Product Managers balance varied perspectives and empower their teams to do great work.

About the Role

When a bank or a hospital loses a critical database to ransomware or a bad change, nobody asks about backup schedules. They ask how fast it's back and whether they can trust what came back. Your job is to make Rubrik the answer to both questions for Oracle.

You'll join the Databases product team with Oracle as your first focus, and own it end to end, from strategy to the outcomes customers see. Oracle is one of the hardest workloads we protect. Our customers run their most important systems on it. You'll also lead work that spans several databases, with the PMs who own them as partners.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Director of Product Management, Databases. You'll work with engineering teams in the US and India.

What You'll Do

  • Own the Oracle roadmap. Set how Rubrik protects and recovers Oracle across RAC, Exadata, Data Guard, on-premises and cloud. Weigh recovery speed against data loss and effort, and make the call.
  • Be the product voice with customers. Run deep dives with DBAs, present to executives when the stakes are high, and explain where Rubrik fits next to Oracle's own tools and other vendors.
  • Turn escalations into product. When a restore matters, you're on the call for product, alongside support, engineering and the customer's DBAs and executives. Bring a plan, then fix the cause in the product.
  • Drive work across databases. Lead initiatives that span several databases, such as recovering whole applications in the right order and proving that backups restore, and help decide which databases we protect next.
  • Choose with evidence. Use customer conversations, usage and support data to make the business case for what to build and what to defer. Write requirements engineers trust, with your reasoning shown.
  • Launch and land. Give sales engineers the positioning and training they need, and join the field on large enterprise deals. Work with partners such as Oracle and Everpure, and track adoption after launch.

What Success Looks Like

  • In 3 months, you've met customers, sales engineers and support. You know where Oracle protection works well and where customers need more, and you've written your view of the roadmap.
  • In 6 months, you're the go-to person for Oracle at Rubrik, and your roadmap shapes what engineering builds.
  • In 12 months, you've shipped improvements Oracle customers notice. You're leading a cross-database initiative with engineering, and you've fixed the root cause of a problem customers kept raising.

What You'll Bring

  • Hands-on experience with Oracle backup and recovery. You can explain how RMAN backups, archived redo logs and point-in-time recovery work, and what Data Guard and RAC change. You've run Oracle in production, supported it or built products for it, and you can go deep on architecture with engineers.
  • Typically 8+ years of product management for technical enterprise products, or equivalent years as a DBA, solutions architect or sales engineer whose calls changed what a team built or bought. You don't need a PM title, but tell us what you changed.
  • Comfort in front of customers at every level, from a room of DBAs to a CIO.
  • Clear, precise writing and speaking. You can turn a messy situation into a short doc that gets a decision.
  • A zero-to-one mindset. You'll write the plan for work that doesn't have one yet, and do what needs doing whatever your title says.
  • Fluency with AI tools in how you research and write.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Exadata, Oracle Database Appliance, or Oracle Database on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), AWS or Azure.
  • Experience with other enterprise databases, such as SQL Server, PostgreSQL or Db2.
  • Background in data protection, disaster recovery or cyber resilience.
  • Experience working with customers in banking, insurance, healthcare or government.

You may not match every line. If you've owned recovery for another enterprise database or for storage, and you've worked with Oracle, apply and tell us how you'd learn the rest.

jobs.title: AI Engineer Intern - Fury Team (Summer 2027)
jobs.description_html:
The future of defense will be decided by those who field intelligent machines at scale. At Scout, we’re developing Fury, the first robotic foundation model for defense, to give U.S. forces overwhelming, adaptable, and autonomous power across every domain. Fury enables human operators to command fleets of robots through natural language, and empowers those machines to sense, decide, and act together as one. It’s not just a leap in autonomy, it’s a force multiplier built for real-world conflict. This mission will ask everything of us: urgency, precision, and relentless work.

The Role

We’re seeking an AI Engineer Intern for Summer 2027 who is passionate about machine learning, robotics, and the future of autonomous systems. As part of the Fury Team, you'll work alongside leading AI and robotics engineers to prototype and test cutting-edge multimodal models that will become the cognitive engine of our robotic platforms. Your work will run on robots in complex, adversarial environments. Expect to move fast, test ideas aggressively, and break new ground as we create the first robotic foundation model for defense.

This 10-week internship is ideal for students looking to apply their research and engineering skills to high-stakes, real-world applications. You’ll gain exposure to the full AI stack, from perception to control, and work on models that run in real world environments.

What You’ll Do

  • Support the design, training, and evaluation of state-of-the-art VLA models for robotic systems

  • Help develop and test scalable ML architectures for perception, robotic actuation, multi-agent coordination, and multi-step reasoning

  • Build model experimentation and evaluation pipelines, utilizing synthetic data gen, simulation, and benchmarking environments

  • Translate research insights into code, experiments, and tests for embodied agents

  • Collaborate with mentors and team members on AI model integration and realtime performance tuning

  • Participate in and help plan data collection and model testing on real robotic hardware and simulation platforms

  • Track, digest, and incorporate breakthroughs from the latest literature in VLMs, RL, CV, and autonomous agents

  • Support field trials and mission operations to validate model performance under real-world constraints

Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, AI, or a related field

  • Strong programming skills in Python, and experience with PyTorch or TensorFlow or JAX

  • Familiarity with deep learning application to at least one of: control policies, visual understanding, language modeling, or reinforcement learning

  • Comfortable navigating open-ended problems and proposing technical solutions

  • Bonus: Experience with robotics or real-time systems

  • Bonus: Experience training models on large-scale compute resources

  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

About SecurityScorecard:

SecurityScorecard is the global leader in cybersecurity ratings, with over 12 million companies continuously rated, operating in 64 countries. Founded in 2013 by security and risk experts Dr. Alex Yampolskiy and Sam Kassoumeh and funded by world-class investors, SecurityScorecard’s patented rating technology is used by over 25,000 organizations for self-monitoring, third-party risk management, board reporting, and cyber insurance underwriting; making all organizations more resilient by allowing them to easily find and fix cybersecurity risks across their digital footprint. 

Headquartered in New York City, our culture has been recognized by Inc Magazine as a "Best Workplace,” by Crain’s NY as a "Best Places to Work in NYC," and as one of the 10 hottest SaaS startups in New York for two years in a row. Most recently, SecurityScorecard was named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies for 2023 and to the Achievers 50 Most Engaged Workplaces in 2023 award recognizing “forward-thinking employers for their unwavering commitment to employee engagement.”  SecurityScorecard is proud to be funded by world-class investors including Silver Lake Waterman, Moody’s, Sequoia Capital, GV and Riverwood Capital.

About the Role:

We’re reorganizing engineering into 16 to 18 small squads grouped under five technical domains. Each domain has a lead who stays hands-on in the code, and squad leads keep their engineering titles and spend at least half their time building. There’s no director layer between them and the VP of Engineering, which keeps decisions close to the work. The tradeoff is that nobody is currently coordinating across squads. You’ll be that person.

This is the first and only TPM inside engineering, reporting to the VP of Engineering. You’ll own whether cross-domain programs are visible and on track: which squad blocks which, what has to land before what, and where the technical dependencies sit. Then you’ll automate as much of that as you can, so coordination scales with the number of teams instead of growing with them.

You won’t have direct reports, and you won’t own product or technical decisions. Domain and squad leads own delivery, and product owns what gets built. Your leverage is clarity: the right information in front of the right people before something slips. If you need a team under you or a title to get things done, this role won’t be a good fit.

We already have a PMO that tracks programs at the portfolio level. You won’t duplicate it. You’ll work inside engineering, at the level of squads and technical dependencies, and the PMO will get better inputs because of it.

What You’ll Do

  • Own tracking for every program that crosses squad or domain lines, from kickoff until it lands.
  • Map dependencies between squads before work starts, keep the map current, and flag risk early enough for leads to act on it.
  • Build the status and visibility system for engineering: what gets tracked, where, and how leadership sees it without asking.
  • Automate the coordination work. Use Jira, dashboards, scripts, and AI agents so status, dependency alerts, and reporting happen without anyone chasing them.
  • Run the cross-team communication squads depend on: planning syncs, sequencing reviews, and readable written updates.
  • Chase things down. When a dependency stalls, find out why, get the right leads talking, and escalate to the VP when they can’t resolve it.
  • Feed the PMO clean, accurate engineering inputs for portfolio-level reporting.
  • Support managers running quarter-long champion initiatives outside their squads with lightweight tracking and goal reviews.
  • Measure whether coordination is getting cheaper as the team count grows, and change the system when it isn’t.
  • Write down how cross-team work runs here so new squads can plug in without a walkthrough.

Who You’ll Work With

You’re accountable for programs being visible and on track, not for the work landing.

  • VP of Engineering: Owns escalations, org structure, and people decisions. You own the full cross-domain picture and surfacing what needs their call.
  • Domain leads: Own sequencing of which squads build what and the interfaces between domains. You own the dependency map and early warning when sequencing breaks.
  • Squad leads: Own specs, implementation, and delivery. You own status that updates itself, so they spend their time building.
  • Architecture: Owns cross-domain design and standards. You own tracking cross-domain technical work to completion.
  • Product managers: Own what gets built and why. You own turning those priorities into a sequenced, visible plan across squads.
  • PMO: Owns portfolio-level tracking and reporting. You own the accuracy of the engineering inputs they receive.

Required Qualifications:

  • 8+ years in program or project management in engineering or technology organizations
  • 3+ years at a B2B SaaS company.
  • Evidence you built the coordination system, not just ran one. Tell us about tools and processes you put in place that outlasted your tenure.
  • Experience in fast-growing or changing organizations where structure was still being defined.
  • Enough technical depth to understand dependencies, architecture tradeoffs, and the SDLC, and to be taken seriously by engineers. No CS degree or coding requirement.
  • Expert in Jira and comfortable administering it, plus dashboards and reporting tools.
  • Hands-on use of AI tools to automate tracking, summarize status, or surface risk, with clear opinions about what works and what doesn’t.
  • A track record of influence without authority: moving senior engineers, managers, and product leads with no reporting line.
  • Flexibility on methodology. You may have strong views, but you work with how each team operates rather than imposing a framework.
  • Persistent follow-through with a light touch. You get people to act by building trust and clarity, not by pressure.
  • Clear, direct writing. Your status updates get read, and people act on them.
  • Comfort with ambiguity. You’ll help define the job as the org changes shape.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in cybersecurity, defense, or other security-focused products
  • Programs that crossed hardware, software, and operations boundaries
  • Prior director-level or business operations scope
  • Experience adapting Scrum, Kanban, or other agile practices to how teams actually work
  • Experience building agentic workflows or scripts for delivery reporting

Benefits:

Specific to each country, we offer a competitive salary, stock options, Health benefits, and unlimited PTO, parental leave, tuition reimbursements, and much more!

Actual compensation for the position is based on a variety of factors, including, but not limited to affordability, skills, qualifications and experience, and may vary from the range. In addition to base salary, employees may also be eligible for annual performance-based incentive compensation awards and equity, among other company benefits.

  • For candidates based in U.S. locations, the estimated total compensation range for this position is $180,000 - $240,000 USD (base salary plus bonus).
  • For candidates based in Canada, the estimated total compensation range for this position is $200,000 - $280,000 CAD (base salary plus bonus).

jobs.description_html:
About SecurityScorecard:

SecurityScorecard is the global leader in cybersecurity ratings, with over 12 million companies continuously rated, operating in 64 countries. Founded in 2013 by security and risk experts Dr. Alex Yampolskiy and Sam Kassoumeh and funded by world-class investors, SecurityScorecard’s patented rating technology is used by over 25,000 organizations for self-monitoring, third-party risk management, board reporting, and cyber insurance underwriting; making all organizations more resilient by allowing them to easily find and fix cybersecurity risks across their digital footprint. 

Headquartered in New York City, our culture has been recognized by Inc Magazine as a "Best Workplace,” by Crain’s NY as a "Best Places to Work in NYC," and as one of the 10 hottest SaaS startups in New York for two years in a row. About the Role:

We're looking for a Staff UX Designer who will be the person on our product team closest to the customer. You'll own end-to-end workflows in our third-party risk products: the full path from a security risk surfacing in SecurityScorecard to the moment it's fixed and closed, including what happens on the vendor's side. We judge your work by the outcome for the customer, not the output. A report is an output; a risk leader who walks into their board meeting with every answer ready is an outcome.

We don't have a separate research team. Every designer here is a researcher: you'll be on customer calls, sit with customers while they work, and use AI (we use Claude) to mine call recordings and product data for gaps. You'll also work directly in our codebase, prototyping and building with Claude and opening your own pull requests alongside engineers.

This is a hands-on, senior individual contributor role for someone who would rather do the customer's job for a day than read another dashboard about them.

What You'll Do

  • Walk in the customer's shoes. Do the work our customers do, such as taking a vendor risk finding from discovery through remediation, and design from what you learn.
  • Own workflows end to end. Define where each workflow begins and ends, and design it so customers reach the outcome they need. Follow every action through to the people on the receiving end, including vendors asked to fix an issue, until the work is done.
  • Design systems of action, not just dashboards. Build experiences that move a risk from discovered to fixed and closed, and make it easy for everyone involved to take the next step.
  • Research continuously, with AI. Join customer calls, run working sessions, and use Claude to analyze call recordings, feedback and product usage, then map what you find to the roadmap.
  • Build directly in the codebase. Prototype and build with Claude against our code and design system, and open pull requests yourself.
  • Raise the team's AI practice. Write and share Claude skills in our team repositories so design output stays consistent, and help engineers tokenize our design system so people and agents can build on it.
  • Work across the company. Partner with product, engineering, sales, customer success and marketing, and go find the context you need, whether that's a call recording or a quick question to a customer success manager.
  • Build trusted customer relationships. Spend time with enterprise customers, including senior stakeholders, on site and in live working sessions.
  • Think critically under pressure. When an urgent request lands, clarify the intent behind it, weigh the options, recommend the best path, and still deliver fast.

Required Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of product or UX design experience, including 3+ years designing B2B or enterprise SaaS products with dense data, permissions and multi-step workflows.
  • Regular, direct customer contact: research, site visits or live working sessions, ideally with senior enterprise stakeholders.
  • A portfolio with at least one workflow you designed and shipped from beginning to end, and evidence of what it changed for the customer.
  • Hands-on AI practice in code. You use Claude or a similar tool to build prototypes or components in a real codebase or design system repository, and you've opened pull requests yourself. Be ready to show what you built, how you prompted it, and what you had to fix by hand. General familiarity with AI tools isn't enough.
  • Experience using AI for research: turning customer calls, feedback or usage data into design decisions.
  • Strong product judgment. You ask why, frame the real problem, and recommend a path among options.
  • A record of delivering on tight timelines and adapting when priorities shift.
  • Strong Figma skills and modern interaction design craft. 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience on both enterprise and consumer products, bringing modern consumer-grade interaction patterns into complex B2B software.
  • Experience in cybersecurity, third-party risk management (TPRM), governance, risk and compliance (GRC), or another regulated domain.
  • Contributions to a design system in code, especially a tokenized one.
  • Experience designing AI-powered features that keep users in control when the model is wrong.
  • Front-end code you've shipped (HTML, CSS, components).
  • Accessibility built into your process (WCAG 2.2). 

Who You Are

  • Customer-obsessed. You understand a problem by living it, not by reading about it.
  • A critical thinker. When a request lands, you slow down long enough to understand the intent before you build, and you come back with a recommendation, not just a deliverable.
  • Relentlessly curious. You go find the answer: you listen to the call, ask the person closest to the customer, and keep learning outside your day job.
  • Built for pace. You deliver on tight timelines and roll with shifting priorities, and you ask why when it matters.
  • A teammate who makes others better. You hold a high craft bar, give and seek direct feedback, and stay open and curious when you're challenged.

Benefits:

Specific to each country, we offer a competitive salary, stock options, Health benefits, and unlimited PTO, parental leave, tuition reimbursements, and much more!
